units.zh: 列傳一百六十五
units.en: Biography 165
units.literal: Biographies 165

units.zh: 黃爵滋金應麟陳慶鏞蘇廷魁朱琦
units.en: Huang Juezi, Jin Yinglin, Chen Qingyong, Su Tingkui, and Zhu Qi
units.literal: Huang Juezi, Jin Yinglin, Chen Qingyong, Su Tingkui, Zhu Qi

units.zh: 黃爵滋，字樹齋，江西宜黃人。
units.en: Huang Juezi (style name Shuzhai) came from Yihuang in Jiangxi.
units.literal: Huang Juezi, courtesy name Shuzhai, was a man of Yihuang in Jiangxi.

units.zh: 道光三年進士，選庶吉士，授編修，遷御史、給事中。
units.en: He earned his jinshi degree in Daoguang 3 (1823), entered the Hanlin Academy as a probationary academician, served as a compiling editor, and was later promoted to censor and supervising secretary.
units.literal: In the third year of Daoguang he became a jinshi, was selected as a bachelor of the Hanlin Academy, was appointed compiling editor, and was transferred to censor and supervising secretary.

units.zh: 以直諫負時望，遇事鋒發，無所迴避，言屢被採納。
units.en: He won renown for frank memorials, spoke out sharply on every issue without pulling punches, and saw many of his proposals accepted by the throne.
units.literal: Because of blunt remonstrance he bore contemporary reputation; when matters arose he was sharp and unrestrained and did not evade; his words were repeatedly adopted.

units.zh: 十五年，特擢鴻臚寺卿。
units.en: In Daoguang 15 (1835) he received a special promotion to vice minister of the Court of Imperial Entertainments.
units.literal: In the fifteenth year he was specially promoted to vice minister of the Court of Imperial Entertainments.

units.zh: 詔以爵滋及科道中馮贊勳、金應麟、曾望顏諸人均敢言，故特加擢任，風勵言官，開忠諫之路，勉其勿因驟得升階，即圖保位，並以誥誡臣工焉。
units.en: An edict explained that Juezi, along with supervising secretaries Feng Zanxun, Jin Yinglin, Zeng Wangyan, and others, had all spoken boldly, and were promoted expressly to encourage the censorate and widen the avenue of loyal remonstrance—while warning them not to grow cautious about preserving rank once elevated, a message meant for the bureaucracy at large.
units.literal: An edict stated that because Juezi and among the censors and supervising secretaries Feng Zanxun, Jin Yinglin, Zeng Wangyan, and the rest were all daring in speech, they were therefore specially promoted to encourage censorial officials, open the path of loyal remonstrance, urge them not because of sudden advancement in rank immediately to scheme to preserve their positions, and also to admonish the officials with an imperial pronouncement.

units.zh: 尋疏陳察天道，廣言路，儲將才，制匪民，整飭京城營衛，申嚴外夷防禁六事，又陳漕、河積弊，均下議行。
units.en: He soon submitted memorials on six topics—reading Heaven's signs, widening remonstrance, cultivating military talent, controlling lawless populations, reforming the capital garrisons, and tightening coastal defences against foreigners—along with long-standing abuses in the grain transport and river works; the court referred them all for policy action.
units.literal: Soon after he memorialized on investigating Heaven's way, broadening the avenue of speech, storing up general talent, controlling rebel populace, rectifying the capital's garrison guard, and strictly enforcing foreign-barbarian prohibitions—six matters—and also presented the accumulated abuses of the grain transport and river systems; all were sent down for discussion and implementation.

units.zh: 時英吉利船艦屢至閩、浙、江南、山東洋面遊奕，測繪山川地圖。
units.en: English vessels were then appearing repeatedly off the coasts of Fujian, Zhejiang, Jiangnan, and Shandong, cruising the waters and charting the landscape.
units.literal: At the time English ships repeatedly came to the sea surfaces of Fujian, Zhejiang, Jiangnan, and Shandong on patrol, surveying and mapping mountains, rivers, and terrain.

units.zh: 爵滋疏言：「外國不可盡以恩撫，而沿海無備可危。」
units.en: Juezi warned in a memorial: "Foreign powers cannot be handled solely through conciliation, and our undefended coast is gravely exposed."
units.literal: Juezi memorialized, saying: 'Foreign states cannot all be treated entirely with gracious appeasement, and the coast being unprepared is perilous.'

units.zh: 十八年，上禁煙議疏曰：「竊見近年銀價遞增，每銀一兩，易制錢一千六百有零，非耗銀於內地，實漏銀於外洋也。
units.en: In Daoguang 18 (1838), in his celebrated memorial urging an opium ban, he wrote: "I observe that silver has grown steadily dearer in recent years—each tael now exchanges for over sixteen hundred cash. This is not domestic consumption of silver, but a drain of silver overseas.
units.literal: In the eighteenth year, on the memorial debating prohibition of opium, he said: 'Your servant observes that in recent years the price of silver has risen in succession; for each tael of silver one exchanges more than sixteen hundred standard cash—this is not silver being consumed within the interior, but in truth silver leaking to the outer seas.

units.zh: 蓋自鴉片流入中國，道光三年以前，每歲漏銀數百萬兩，其初不過紈褲子弟習為浮靡。
units.en: Since opium entered China, the annual outflow before Daoguang 3 had already run to several million taels; at first only wealthy young idlers took it up as a fashionable vice.
units.literal: For since opium flowed into China, before the third year of Daoguang each year several million taels of silver leaked out; at first it was no more than silk-trousered sons of good families practicing dissipation.

units.zh: 嗣後上自官府搢紳，下至工商優隸，以及婦女僧道，隨在吸食。
units.en: Soon officials and gentry at the top, artisans and merchants below, actors and servants, even women, monks, and priests were smoking it everywhere.
units.literal: Thereafter, from above officials and gentry down to artisans, merchants, actors, and bond servants, as well as women, monks, and Daoist priests, wherever one went they smoked it.

units.zh: 粵省奸商勾通兵弁，用扒龍、快蟹等船，運銀出洋，運煙入口。
units.en: Guangdong smugglers colluded with soldiers and clerks, using swift craft such as the "dragon-stripping" and "fast crab" boats to ship silver abroad and opium ashore.
units.literal: Wicked merchants of Guangdong province colluded with soldiers and clerks, using 'dragon-stripping' and 'fast crab' and other vessels to transport silver out to sea and transport opium into the ports.

units.zh: 故自道光三年至十一年，歲漏銀一千七八百萬兩；
units.en: From Daoguang 3 to 11, the annual drain ran to seventeen or eighteen million taels;
units.literal: Therefore from the third year of Daoguang to the eleventh, each year seventeen or eighteen million taels of silver leaked out;

units.zh: 十一年至十四年，歲漏銀二千餘萬兩；
units.en: from Daoguang 11 to 14, to more than twenty million taels a year;
units.literal: from the eleventh to the fourteenth year, each year more than twenty million taels leaked;

units.zh: 十四年至今，漸漏至三千萬之多；
units.en: and since Daoguang 14 the figure has climbed toward thirty million;
units.literal: from the fourteenth year to the present, gradually leaking to as much as thirty million;

units.zh: 福建、浙江、山東、天津各海口合之亦數千萬兩。
units.en: while the ports of Fujian, Zhejiang, Shandong, and Tianjin together account for tens of millions more.
units.literal: the various sea mouths of Fujian, Zhejiang, Shandong, and Tianjin combined also amount to tens of millions of taels.

units.zh: 以中土有用之財，填海外無窮之壑，易此害人之物，漸成病國之憂，年復一年，不知伊於胡底。
units.en: China's productive wealth is poured into a bottomless foreign pit in exchange for this poison, and the nation grows sicker year by year with no end in sight.
units.literal: Using the Middle Kingdom's useful wealth to fill the outer seas' bottomless gully, exchanging for this harm-doing substance, gradually it became the worry of a sickening state; year after year, one does not know where it will end.

units.zh: 各省州縣地丁錢糧，徵錢為多，及辦奏銷，以錢為銀，前此多有贏餘，今則無不賠貼。
units.en: Land tax across the provinces was collected chiefly in copper cash, then converted to silver for final accounts—formerly officials often showed a surplus, but now every settlement runs at a loss.
units.literal: In each province's prefectures and counties the land-and-poll tax grain payments were collected mostly in cash; when preparing memorial accounts for clearance, cash was converted to silver—before this there were often surpluses, but now there is none that does not require making up shortfalls.

units.zh: 各省鹽商賣鹽得錢，交課用銀，昔之爭為利藪者，今則視為畏途。
units.en: Salt merchants who once fought for the lucrative salt trade now receive payment in cash but must remit duties in silver—a business once prized has become a path to ruin.
units.literal: In each province salt merchants sold salt and received cash, paid duties in silver—what was once competed over as a profit pool, now is regarded as a road of dread.

units.zh: 若再數年，銀價愈貴，奏銷如何能辦？
units.en: If silver keeps rising for a few more years, how can fiscal settlements possibly be completed?
units.literal: If for several more years the price of silver grows dearer, how can memorial clearance accounts be managed?

units.zh: 積課如何能清？
units.en: How can accumulated tax arrears ever be cleared?
units.literal: How can accumulated tax arrears be cleared?

units.zh: 設有不測之用，又如何能支？
units.en: And if an emergency arose, how could the treasury meet it?
units.literal: Suppose there were unforeseen expenditures—how again could they be sustained?

units.zh: 今天下皆知漏卮在鴉片，而未知所以禁也。
units.en: Everyone knows opium is the leak in the nation's finances, yet no one has found how to stop it.
units.literal: Today all under Heaven know the leaking vessel is in opium, yet do not know the means to prohibit it.

units.zh: 夫耗銀之多，由於販煙之盛；
units.en: The drain of silver stems from the scale of the opium trade;
units.literal: Now the great consumption of silver arises from the flourishing of opium trafficking;

units.zh: 販煙之盛，由於食煙之眾。
units.en: and trafficking flourishes because smokers are so numerous.
units.literal: the flourishing of opium trafficking arises from the multitude of opium smokers.

units.zh: 無吸食自無興販，無興販則外洋之煙自不來矣。
units.en: Without smokers there would be no trade; without trade, foreign opium would not enter China at all.
units.literal: Without smoking there is naturally no rise of trafficking; without rise of trafficking then foreign opium naturally will not come.

units.zh: 宜先重治吸食，臣請皇上准給一年期限戒菸，雖至深之癮，未有不能斷絕者。
units.en: We should strike first at consumption. I beg Your Majesty to allow a one-year grace period for smokers to quit—even the deepest addiction can be broken.
units.literal: It is fitting first to punish smoking heavily; your servant requests that Your Majesty grant approval to give a one-year deadline to quit smoking—even the deepest addiction, there is none that cannot be broken off.

units.zh: 至一年仍然服食，是不奉法之亂民，加之重刑不足卹。
units.en: Anyone still smoking after a year would be a lawless subject deserving no mercy under the severest penalty.
units.literal: If after one year they still consume it, they are lawless populace who do not obey the law; adding heavy punishment is insufficient to pity.

units.zh: 舊例吸煙罪止枷杖，其不指出興販者，罪止杖一百、徒三年，俱系活罪。
units.en: Under existing law, smoking carried only the cangue and beating; failing to denounce traffickers brought a hundred blows and three years' penal servitude—all punishments short of death.
units.literal: Under old statutes the crime of smoking opium was only cangue and beating; those who did not denounce traffickers were punished only with one hundred blows of the staff and three years' penal servitude—all were living punishments.

units.zh: 斷癮之苦，甚於枷杖與徒，故不肯斷絕。
units.en: Withdrawal hurts more than those penalties, so addicts refuse to quit.
units.literal: The suffering of breaking addiction is greater than cangue-beating and penal servitude, therefore they are unwilling to break off.

units.zh: 若罪以死論，臨刑之慘急，苦於斷癮之苟延，臣知其原死於家而不原死於市。
units.en: Make the penalty death, and the terror of execution would outweigh the misery of withdrawal—I know they would rather die at home than on the scaffold.
units.literal: If the crime were judged by death, the misery and urgency at the moment of execution would be more bitter than the lingering survival of breaking addiction; your servant knows they would rather die at home than die in the marketplace.

units.zh: 況我皇上​​雷霆之威，赫然震怒，雖愚頑沉溺之久，自足以發聾振瞶。
units.en: Coupled with Your Majesty's thunderous wrath, even the most stubborn and long-addicted would be shaken awake.
units.literal: Moreover, our Emperor's thunderbolt authority, manifestly shaking with anger—even the long-deafened and long-blinded by stupidity and addiction would be enough to deafen the ears and startle the eyes.

units.zh: 皇上之旨嚴，則奉法之吏肅，犯法之人畏。
units.en: When the imperial will is stern, officials enforce the law rigorously and offenders take heed.
units.literal: When the Emperor's orders are strict, then law-abiding officials are solemn and law-breaking people are fearful.

units.zh: 一年之內，尚未用刑，十已戒其八九。
units.en: Within that year, before a single execution, eight or nine in ten would quit on their own.
units.literal: Within one year, before punishments have yet been applied, eight or nine out of ten will already have quit.

units.zh: 已食者藉國法以保餘生，未食者因炯戒以全身命，止闢之大權，即好生之盛德也。
units.en: Former smokers would be saved by the law; the untainted would be warned off in time—the power to suppress vice is itself the highest mercy.
units.literal: Those who have smoked rely on state law to preserve the remainder of life; those who have not smoked, through bright warning, preserve body and life—the great authority to stop evil is precisely the great virtue of cherishing life.

units.zh: 伏請飭諭各督撫嚴行清查保甲，初先曉諭，定於一年後取具五家互結，準令舉發，給予優獎。
units.en: I beg Your Majesty to order every governor to enforce the baojia household registers: first instruct the people, then after one year require mutual guarantees from groups of five households, allow informers to come forward with generous rewards,
units.literal: Your servant respectfully requests ordering each governor-general and governor to strictly carry out investigation through the baojia system, first instructing and explaining, fixing that after one year they obtain mutual guarantees from five households, permitting denunciation, and granting excellent rewards.

units.zh: 倘有容隱，本犯照新例處死，互結之家照例治罪。
units.en: and if anyone is concealed, execute the offender under the new statute and punish the guaranteeing households as well.
units.literal: if there is concealment, the principal offender is executed according to the new statute, and the mutually guaranteeing households are punished according to precedent.

units.zh: 通都大邑，往來客商，責成店鋪，如有容留食煙之人，照窩藏匪類治罪。
units.en: In major cities and trading towns, hold inns responsible: any shop that harbors smokers should be punished as for sheltering criminals.
units.literal: In great cities and major towns, for traveling merchants coming and going, charge the shops with responsibility; if they harbor persons who smoke opium, punish according to the statute for harboring bandit types.

units.zh: 文武大小各官，照常人加等，子孫不准考試。
units.en: Civil and military officials of every rank should face aggravated penalties, and their descendants should be barred from the examinations.
units.literal: Civil and military officials great and small, compared with ordinary people with increased grade; their sons and grandsons are not permitted to sit for examinations.

units.zh: 官親幕友家丁，除本犯治罪外，本管官嚴加議處。
units.en: For relatives, secretaries, and servants of officials, punish the offenders and also hold the supervising official strictly accountable.
units.literal: Officials' kin, secretaries, and household servants—besides punishing the principal offenders, the supervising official is strictly subject to deliberation and disposition.

units.zh: 滿、漢官兵，照地方官保甲辦理；
units.en: Manchu and Han troops should be registered and policed through the baojia system like civilians;
units.literal: Manchu and Han military officers and soldiers are to be handled according to the local officials' baojia procedures;

units.zh: 管轄失察之人，照地方官辦理。
units.en: and commanders who fail to detect offenders should face the same penalties as civil officials.
units.literal: those in jurisdiction who fail in supervision are handled according to local officials' procedures.

units.zh: 庶幾軍民一體，上下肅清，漏卮可塞，銀價不至再昂，然後講求理財之方，誠天下萬世臣民之福也。」
units.en: Then army and people alike would be cleansed, the fiscal leak plugged, and silver might cease its rise—only then could we truly reform the finances. That would be a blessing for the empire and for generations to come."
units.literal: Perhaps then military and populace will be one body, above and below will be cleared, the leaking vessel can be stopped, the price of silver will not rise again, and only then can methods of managing finances be sought—truly the blessing of all under Heaven for ten thousand generations of subjects.'

units.zh: 疏上，上深韙之，下疆臣各抒所見，速議章程。
units.en: When the memorial reached the throne, the Emperor strongly endorsed it and ordered provincial officials to submit opinions and draft regulations without delay.
units.literal: When the memorial went up, the Emperor deeply approved it, sent it down to frontier officials each to express their views, and urgently debated regulations.

units.zh: 先是，太常寺少卿許乃濟疏言，煙禁雖嚴，閉關不可，徒法不行，請仍用舊制納稅，以貨易貨，不得用銀購買，吸食罪名，專重官員、士子、兵丁，時皆謂非政體。
units.en: Earlier, Xu Naiji of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices had argued that strict prohibition was unworkable while the coast remained closed to trade, and proposed legalizing opium under the old tax system with barter instead of silver payment and heavier penalties only for officials, scholars, and soldiers—a plan widely condemned as improper.
units.literal: Earlier, Vice Minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices Xu Naiji memorialized, saying that although the opium ban was strict, closing the frontier was impossible; the law alone would not be carried out; he requested still using the old system of paying tax, exchanging goods for goods, not permitting purchase with silver; the crime of smoking would weigh especially on officials, scholars, and soldiers—at the time all said this was not proper state policy.

units.zh: 爵滋劾乃濟，罷其職，連擢爵滋大理寺少卿、通政使、禮部侍郎，調刑部。
units.en: Juezi impeached Xu Naiji, who was dismissed; Juezi was then promoted in rapid succession to vice minister of the Court of Judicial Review, transmission commissioner, vice minister of Rites, and finally transferred to the Ministry of Punishments.
units.literal: Juezi impeached Naiji and he was dismissed from office; Juezi was continuously promoted to vice minister of the Court of Judicial Review, commissioner of the Office of Transmission, vice minister of Rites, and transferred to the Ministry of Punishments.

units.zh: 十九年，廷臣議定販煙、吸煙罪名新例，略如爵滋所請。
units.en: In Daoguang 19 (1839), the court enacted new statutes on trafficking and smoking opium, largely along the lines Juezi had proposed.
units.literal: In the nineteenth year, court ministers deliberated and fixed new statutes for the crimes of trafficking and smoking opium, broadly like what Juezi had requested.

units.zh: 林則徐至粵，盡焚躉船存煙，議外國人販煙罪。
units.en: Lin Zexu reached Guangdong, burned all the opium stored on the receiving ships, and pressed charges against foreign traffickers.
units.literal: Lin Zexu arrived in Guangdong, completely burned the stored opium on the receiving ships, and deliberated the crime of foreigners trafficking opium.

units.zh: 英領事義律不就約束，兵釁遂開。
units.en: The British consul Charles Elliot refused to comply, and war broke out.
units.literal: The English consul Elliot did not submit to restraint, and military hostilities thereupon opened.

units.zh: 二十年，命爵滋偕左都御史祁俊藻赴福建查辦禁煙，與總督鄧廷楨籌備海防。
units.en: In Daoguang 20 (1840), Juezi was sent with Left Censor-in-Chief Qi Junzao to Fujian to oversee the opium ban and, with Governor-General Deng Tingzhen, to prepare coastal defences.
units.literal: In the twentieth year, Juezi was ordered together with Left Censor-in-Chief Qi Junzao to go to Fujian to investigate and handle prohibition of opium, and with Governor-General Deng Tingzhen to plan coastal defense.

units.zh: 洎英兵來犯，廷楨屢挫敵於廈門，上疑之。
units.en: When British forces attacked, Deng Tingzhen reported repeated victories at Xiamen, which the Emperor found hard to believe.
units.literal: When English troops came to attack, Tingzhen repeatedly defeated the enemy at Xiamen; the Emperor was suspicious.

units.zh: 爵滋與俊藻方至浙江按事，復命赴福建察奏。
units.en: Juezi and Qi Junzao were inspecting affairs in Zhejiang when they were ordered back to Fujian to investigate and report.
units.literal: Juezi and Junzao had just reached Zhejiang on an inspection mission when they were again ordered to go to Fujian to investigate and memorialize.

units.zh: 疏陳：「廷楨所奏不誣；
units.en: They reported: "Deng Tingzhen's accounts were not false;
units.literal: They memorialized, stating: 'What Tingzhen reported is not false;

units.zh: 定海不可不速復；
units.en: Dinghai must be recovered without delay;
units.literal: Dinghai cannot but be swiftly recovered;

units.zh: 水師有專門之技，宜破格用人。」
units.en: and the navy's specialized skills require appointing men outside the usual seniority rules."
units.literal: the navy has specialized skills—it is fitting to employ men outside normal rules.'

units.zh: 具言戰守方略。
units.en: They laid out detailed plans for offense and defense.
units.literal: They fully set forth strategies for fighting and defense.

units.zh: 又言浙江為閩、粵之心腹，與江蘇為脣齒，請飭伊里布不可偏聽琦善，信敵必退。
units.en: They also warned that Zhejiang was the strategic heart linking Fujian and Guangdong to Jiangsu, and urged the court to tell Yilibu not to heed Qishan alone or assume the enemy would simply withdraw.
units.literal: They also said Zhejiang was the heart and belly of Fujian and Guangdong, and with Jiangsu was lip and teeth; they requested ordering Yilibu not to listen one-sidedly to Qishan and believe the enemy would certainly withdraw.

units.zh: 及回京，復極言英人勞師襲遠不足慮，宜竟與絕市，募兵節餉，為持久計，以海防圖進。
units.en: Back in Beijing, Juezi argued forcefully that Britain's expeditionary forces were overextended, urged a complete trade embargo, recruitment and fiscal retrenchment for a war of attrition, and submitted a coastal defence map.
units.literal: When they returned to the capital, they again spoke at length that the English, laboring their armies to strike from afar, were not worth worrying about; it was fitting to cut off trade entirely, raise troops and economize supplies, make long-term plans, and present a coastal defense map.

units.zh: 既而琦善在粵議撫不得要領，連歲命將出師，廣東、浙江皆不利。
units.en: Qishan's peace negotiations in Guangdong then failed, and repeated campaigns in Guangdong and Zhejiang went badly.
units.literal: Soon after, Qishan in Guangdong negotiated appeasement without grasping essentials; year after year generals were ordered to take the field; in Guangdong and Zhejiang all were unfavorable.

units.zh: 二十二年，英兵由海入江，乃定和議於江寧，煙禁自此弛矣。
units.en: In Daoguang 22 (1842), British forces advanced up the Yangzi from the sea, and peace was concluded at Nanjing—the opium prohibition was effectively abandoned.
units.literal: In the twenty-second year, English troops entered the Yangzi from the sea; the peace treaty was then fixed at Jiangning, and from this the opium ban was relaxed.

units.zh: 尋丁父憂去官。
units.en: He soon resigned to observe mourning for his father.
units.literal: Soon after he entered mourning for his father and left office.

units.zh: 爵滋為御史時，稽察戶部銀庫，嘗疏言庫丁輕收虧帑之弊。
units.en: As a censor, Juezi had inspected the Ministry of Revenue silver vault and memorialized on clerks who accepted short payments and caused treasury losses.
units.literal: When Juezi was a censor, he inspected the Ministry of Revenue silver vault and once memorialized on the abuse of vault clerks lightly receiving payments and causing treasury deficits.

units.zh: 二十三年，銀庫虧空九百萬兩事發，追論管庫、查庫諸臣，罪皆褫職責賠，賠既足，次第予官。
units.en: In Daoguang 23 (1843), a nine-million-tael vault deficit came to light; vault managers and inspectors were stripped of rank and ordered to make restitution, and were gradually reappointed once they had paid in full.
units.literal: In the twenty-third year, the matter of a nine-million-tael deficit in the silver vault broke out; retrospectively the vault-managing and vault-inspecting officials were judged—all were stripped of office and ordered to compensate; once compensation was complete, offices were granted in succession.

units.zh: 爵滋以員外郎候補，病足家居，上猶時問其何在。
units.en: Juezi awaited appointment as a vice director but stayed home with a foot ailment; the Emperor still occasionally inquired after him.
units.literal: Juezi awaited appointment as an outside-section vice director; ill in the foot, he remained at home, yet the Emperor still occasionally asked where he was.

units.zh: 三十年，至京，會上崩，遂不出。
units.en: He came to Beijing in Daoguang 30 (1850), but the Emperor died soon after, and he never took office again.
units.literal: In the thirtieth year he reached the capital; it happened that the Emperor died, and he therefore did not go out.

units.zh: 逾三年，卒。
units.en: He died three years later.
units.literal: After more than three years, he died.

units.zh: 爵滋以詩名，喜交遊，每夜閉閣草奏，日騎出，遍視諸故人名士，飲酒賦詩，意氣豪甚。
units.en: Juezi was known as a poet and a convivial man: he drafted memorials by night, rode out by day to visit friends and literati, drinking and composing verse with exuberant spirit.
units.literal: Juezi was famed for poetry and delighted in socializing; each night he closed his study to draft memorials, by day rode out, visited all his old friends and famous scholars everywhere, drinking wine and composing poetry—his spirit was very bold.

units.zh: 及創議禁煙，始終主戰，一時以為清流眉目。
units.en: When he launched the drive to ban opium he consistently favored war, and for a time was seen as the moral leader of the Qingliu reform party.
units.literal: When he initiated the proposal to ban opium, he always advocated war; for a time he was regarded as the leading figure of the moralist faction.

units.zh: 所著奏議、詩文集行於世。
units.en: His collected memorials, poetry, and prose circulated widely.
units.literal: His collected memorials and poetry and prose circulated in the world.

units.zh: 金應麟，字亞伯，浙江錢塘人。
units.en: Jin Yinglin (style name Yabo) came from Qiantang in Zhejiang.
units.literal: Jin Yinglin, courtesy name Yabo, was a man of Qiantang in Zhejiang.

units.zh: 以舉人入貲為中書。
units.en: As a provincial graduate he purchased appointment as a secretariat drafter.
units.literal: As a provincial graduate he purchased office and became a secretary in the Grand Secretariat.

units.zh: 道光六年，成進士，授刑部主事，總辦秋審，先後從大臣讞獄四川、湖北、山西。
units.en: He passed the jinshi examination in Daoguang 6 (1826), was made a principal clerk in the Ministry of Punishments, supervised the autumn judicial review, and accompanied senior officials on case reviews in Sichuan, Hubei, and Shanxi.
units.literal: In the sixth year of Daoguang he became a jinshi, was appointed a principal clerk in the Ministry of Punishments, supervised the autumn assizes, and successively followed senior ministers in reviewing cases in Sichuan, Hubei, and Shanxi.

units.zh: 累擢郎中，改御史，遷給事中。
units.en: He rose through the ranks to director, then censor, then supervising secretary.
units.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to director, transferred to censor, and moved to supervising secretary.

units.zh: 疏請修改刑例，於鬥毆、報盜、劫囚、誣告、私鑄、服舍違式、斷罪引律、奴婢毆主、故禁故勘平人、應捕人追捕罪人、犯罪存留養親、官司出入人罪、徒流遷徙地方、外省駐防逃人，逐條論列，多被採取改定；
units.en: He memorialized for revisions to the penal code, addressing affray, reporting bandits, prison breaks, false accusation, private coining, mourning and residence violations, sentencing citations, slaves assaulting masters, wrongful imprisonment and torture, authorized pursuit of criminals, retention for filial support, official misconduct in criminal cases, places of exile, and fugitives from provincial garrisons—article by article; many of his proposals were adopted;
units.literal: He memorialized requesting revision of the penal code, on affray, reporting bandits, rescuing prisoners, false accusation, private coining, violation of mourning and residence regulations, citing statutes in sentencing, slaves and maids beating masters, wrongful imprisonment and torture of commoners, authorized pursuers chasing criminals, crimes with retention for supporting parents, officials improperly entering or releasing persons in crimes, places of penal servitude and exile, and escaped bondsmen in provincial garrisons—discussing each article in turn; many were adopted and revised;

units.zh: 又論銅船恣橫不法及驛站擾累諸弊，並下各省督撫禁革。
units.en: he also exposed abuses by copper-transport boats and the burdens imposed by the courier stations, and the court ordered provincial governors to suppress them.
units.literal: he also discussed the abuses of copper-transport ships acting lawlessly and post stations causing harassment and burdens—all were sent down to each province's governors for prohibition and reform.

units.zh: 先後封事數十上，劾疆臣琦善、河臣吳邦慶尤為時稱。
units.en: He submitted dozens of confidential memorials in all; his impeachments of Governor-General Qishan and river conservancy official Wu Bangqing won particular acclaim.
units.literal: In succession he submitted several tens of confidential memorials; his impeachments of frontier official Qishan and river official Wu Bangqing were especially praised by the times.

units.zh: 宣宗嘉其敢言，擢太常寺少卿。
units.en: The Daoguang Emperor praised his outspokenness and promoted him to vice minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
units.literal: The Xuanzong Emperor commended his daring speech and promoted him to vice minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

units.zh: 遭憂歸，服闋，授鴻臚寺卿。
units.en: After a period of mourning he was appointed vice minister of the Court of Imperial Entertainments.
units.literal: He entered mourning and returned home; when mourning ended he was appointed vice minister of the Court of Imperial Entertainments.

units.zh: 疏論水師廢弛，漕政頹紊。
units.en: He memorialized on the decay of the navy and the disorder of the grain transport system.
units.literal: He memorialized on the navy's lax discipline and the grain transport administration's decline and disorder.

units.zh: 十九年，出為直隸按察使，鞫護理長蘆鹽運使楊成業等得贓獄，論遣戍，前運使陳崇禮等並罣議。
units.en: In Daoguang 19 he was posted as surveillance commissioner of Zhili, tried Acting Changlu Salt Transport Commissioner Yang Chengye and others for bribery, sentenced them to exile, and implicated former transport commissioners including Chen Chongli.
units.literal: In the nineteenth year he went out as surveillance commissioner of Zhili, tried Acting Changlu Salt Transport Commissioner Yang Chengye and others in a bribery case, sentenced them to banishment, and former transport commissioners Chen Chongli and others were also implicated in deliberation.

units.zh: 尋召為大理寺少卿。
units.en: He was soon recalled as vice minister of the Court of Judicial Review.
units.literal: Soon after he was recalled as vice minister of the Court of Judicial Review.

units.zh: 二十二年，疏言：「海疆諸臣欺罔，其故由於爵祿之念重，而趨避之計工。
units.en: In Daoguang 22 he wrote: "Coastal officials deceive the throne because they prize rank and salary above all and are skilled at evasion.
units.literal: In the twenty-second year he memorialized, saying: 'Coastal officials deceive and mislead; the reason lies in the thought of rank and salary being heavy, while schemes of evasion and avoidance are skillful.

units.zh: 欲破其欺，是在乾斷。
units.en: To break their deceit requires resolute imperial decision.
units.literal: To break their deception lies in resolute decision.

units.zh: 資格不可拘，嫌疑不必避，舊過不妨宥，重賞不宜惜。
units.en: Do not be bound by seniority, do not shrink from suspicion, pardon past faults, and do not stint on rewards.
units.literal: Seniority must not be constrained, suspicion need not be avoided, old faults may be pardoned, heavy rewards should not be spared.

units.zh: 近頃長江海口鎮兵足守，而敵船深入，逃潰時聞。
units.en: Recently at the Yangzi estuary the garrison was ample on paper, yet enemy ships penetrated deep inland and rout was reported again and again.
units.literal: Recently at the Yangzi estuary garrison troops were sufficient to defend, yet enemy ships penetrated deeply, and flight and rout were heard from time to time.

units.zh: 竭億萬氓庶之脂膏。
units.en: The fat of the people is drained dry
units.literal: Exhausting the fat and cream of billions of common people.

units.zh: 保一二庸臣之軀命。
units.en: to preserve the lives of a few mediocre officials.
units.literal: to preserve the bodies and lives of one or two mediocre officials.

units.zh: 議者諉謂無人無兵無餉無械。
units.en: Critics excuse failure by claiming there are no men, no troops, no funds, and no weapons.
units.literal: Discussants shifted blame, saying there were no men, no troops, no funds, no weapons.

units.zh: 竊以無人當求，無兵當練，無餉械亦當計度固有，多則持重，少則用謀，作三軍之氣，定邊疆之危，在皇上假以事權，與任事者運用一心而已。」
units.en: I hold that men must be found, troops must be trained, and funds and arms must be deployed as available—use strength when plentiful, stratagem when scarce, rouse the army's spirit, and secure the frontier. All this requires only that Your Majesty delegate authority and that those in charge act in concert."
units.literal: Your servant holds that if there are no men they should be sought, if no troops they should be drilled; if no funds or weapons, one should also plan what is inherently available—if many, hold firm; if few, use stratagem; rousing the spirit of the three armies and settling frontier peril lies only in the Emperor lending executive authority and the responsible officials operating with one mind.'

units.zh: 复疏進預計度支圖、火器圖、籌海戰方略甚悉。
units.en: He also submitted detailed diagrams of projected revenue and expenditure, firearms, and coastal warfare strategy.
units.literal: He again memorialized, presenting advance budget diagrams, firearms diagrams, and coastal warfare plans in great detail.

units.zh: 二十三年，以親老乞歸省，不復出。
units.en: In Daoguang 23 he asked leave to care for his aged parents and never returned to office.
units.literal: In the twenty-third year, because his parents were aged he requested leave to return home to visit them and did not go out again.

units.zh: 著有廌華堂奏議及駢體文。
units.en: He left behind the Zhihua Hall Memorials and works in parallel prose.
units.literal: He authored the Zhihua Hall Memorials and parallel prose.

units.zh: 陳慶鏞，字頌南，福建晉江人。
units.en: Chen Qingyong (style name Songnan) came from Jinjiang in Fujian.
units.literal: Chen Qingyong, courtesy name Songnan, was a man of Jinjiang in Fujian.

units.zh: 道光十二年進士，選庶吉士，散館授戶部主事，遷員外郎，授御史。
units.en: He earned his jinshi in Daoguang 12 (1832), entered the Hanlin Academy, was posted to the Ministry of Revenue as a principal clerk, rose to vice director, and was made a censor.
units.literal: In the twelfth year of Daoguang he became a jinshi, was selected as a Hanlin bachelor, on leaving the academy was appointed principal clerk in the Ministry of Revenue, was promoted to outside-section vice director, and was appointed censor.

units.zh: 二十三年，海疆僨事，獲罪諸臣浸復起用。
units.en: In Daoguang 23, after the coastal disasters, officials who had been punished were gradually brought back into service.
units.literal: In the twenty-third year, when coastal affairs went awry, the various officials who had been punished were gradually reemployed.

units.zh: 慶鏞上疏論刑賞失措，曰：「行政之要，莫大於刑賞。
units.en: Chen Qingyong memorialized that rewards and punishments had been mishandled: "Nothing matters more in government than how punishments and rewards are applied.
units.literal: Qingyong memorialized on the misplacement of punishments and rewards, saying: 'The essential of administering government is nothing greater than punishments and rewards.

units.zh: 刑賞之權，操之於君，喻之於民，所以示天下之大公也。
units.en: That authority rests with the sovereign and must be made clear to the people, for it embodies the empire's fundamental fairness.
units.literal: The authority of punishments and rewards is wielded by the ruler and explained to the people—thereby showing the great impartiality of all under Heaven.

units.zh: 大學論平天下之道，在於絜矩。
units.en: The Great Learning teaches that bringing peace to the realm depends on holding the measuring square—applying the same standard to oneself that one applies to others.
units.literal: The Great Learning discusses the Way of pacifying all under Heaven—it lies in measuring the square.

units.zh: 矩者何，民之好惡是已。
units.en: What is the measuring square? The people's likes and dislikes.
units.literal: What is the square? It is the people's likes and dislikes—that is all.

units.zh: 海疆多事以來，自總督、將軍以至州縣丞倅，禽駭獸奔。
units.en: Since the coastal troubles began, governors-general, generals, and officials down to county deputies have fled in panic like startled birds and beasts.
units.literal: Since coastal affairs became numerous, from governors-general and generals down to prefectural and county assistants, they were like birds startled and beasts fleeing.

units.zh: 皇上赫然震怒，失律之罪，法有莫逭。
units.en: The Emperor was furious, and the law allowed no escape for those who had broken discipline.
units.literal: The Emperor manifestly shook with anger; the crime of violating discipline—under the law none could escape.

units.zh: 於是辱國之將軍奕山、奕經，參贊文蔚，總督牛鑑，提督餘步雲，先後就逮，步雲伏法。
units.en: The disgraced generals Yishan and Yijing, staff officer Wenwei, Governor-General Niu Jian, and Provincial Commander Yu Buyun were arrested in turn; Buyun was executed.
units.literal: Thereupon the generals who disgraced the state—Yishan, Yijing, the staff officer Wenwei, Governor-General Niu Jian, and Provincial Commander Yu Buyun—were successively arrested; Buyun was executed according to law.

units.zh: 血氣之倫，罔不拊手稱快，謂國法前雖未伸於琦善，今猶伸於餘步雲。
units.en: Men of spirit applauded, saying that although the law had not reached Qishan before, it had at least been applied to Yu Buyun.
units.literal: Men of hot blood, none did not clap hands and call it satisfying, saying that although state law before had not been applied to Qishan, now it was still applied to Yu Buyun.

units.zh: 乃未幾起琦善為葉爾羌幫辦大臣。
units.en: Before long, however, Qishan was reappointed assistant commissioner at Yarkand.
units.literal: Yet before long Qishan was raised as assistant commissioner at Yarkand.

units.zh: 邸報既傳，人情震駭，猶解之曰：'古聖王之待罪人，有投四裔以御魑魅者。
units.en: When the court gazette announced this, the public was appalled, though some explained it by saying that ancient sage kings had banished criminals to the four corners of the realm to ward off evil spirits.
units.literal: Once the court gazette spread, popular feeling was shaken with horror; yet people still explained it, saying: 'The ancient sage kings' treatment of criminals included casting them to the four borderlands to ward off demons.'

units.zh: '皇上之於琦善，殆其類是，而今且以三品頂戴用為熱河都統矣，且用奕經為葉爾羌幫辦大臣，文蔚為古城領隊大臣矣。
units.en: Perhaps the Emperor's treatment of Qishan was of that kind—yet now he was appointed Rehe lieutenant-general with third-rank insignia, Yijing was made Yarkand assistant commissioner, and Wenwei leading commissioner at Gucheng.
units.literal: The Emperor's treatment of Qishan was perhaps of that kind—yet now he was employed as Rehe lieutenant-general with third-rank hat button, and Yijing was employed as Yarkand assistant commissioner, and Wenwei as leading commissioner at Gucheng.

units.zh: 琦善於戰事方始，首先示弱，以惰軍心，海內糜爛，至於此極。
units.en: Qishan had been the first to show weakness when war began, sapping army morale and bringing the empire to ruin.
units.literal: Qishan, when hostilities had just begun, was first to show weakness and thereby enervate army morale; within the seas all was rotten, reaching this extreme.

units.zh: 既罷斥終身不齒，猶恐不足饜民心而作士氣。
units.en: Dismissal and lifelong disgrace would scarcely satisfy public outrage or restore military morale.
units.literal: Having been dismissed and for life not ranked among gentlemen, one still fears this is insufficient to satisfy popular hearts and raise military spirit.

units.zh: 奕經之罪，雖較琦善稍減，文蔚之罪，較奕經又減。
units.en: Yijing's guilt was somewhat less than Qishan's, and Wenwei's somewhat less than Yijing's.
units.literal: Yijing's crime, though somewhat less than Qishan's; Wenwei's crime, again somewhat less than Yijing's.

units.zh: 然皇上命將出師，若何慎重。
units.en: Yet how grave a matter it is when the Emperor sends generals to war.
units.literal: Yet when the Emperor orders generals to take the field, how grave the matter.

units.zh: 奕經頓兵半載，曾未身歷行間，騁其虛憍之氣，自詭一鼓而復三城；
units.en: Yijing kept his army idle for half a year without ever seeing battle, boasted emptily that one assault would recover three cities,
units.literal: Yijing halted his army for half a year, never personally experienced the battle line, gave rein to his empty arrogance, and falsely claimed that with one drumbeat he would recover three cities;

units.zh: 卒之機事不密，貽笑敵人，覆軍殺將，一敗不支。
units.en: then let his plans leak, made himself a laughingstock to the enemy, lost his army and his generals, and collapsed in a single defeat.
units.literal: in the end his plans were not secret, he gave the enemy cause for laughter, the army was overthrown and generals killed, and one defeat could not be sustained.

units.zh: 此不待別科騷擾供億、招權納賄之罪，而已不可勝誅。
units.en: Without even counting his harassment of the people, waste of supplies, abuse of power, and acceptance of bribes, his crimes were already beyond measure.
units.literal: Without waiting for separate counts of harassing the populace, provisioning expenses, grasping power, and accepting bribes, already his crimes were beyond execution.

units.zh: 臣亦知奕經為高宗純皇帝之裔，皇上親親睦族，不忍遽加顯戮。
units.en: I know that Yijing is a descendant of the Qianlong Emperor, and that Your Majesty, cherishing imperial kin, is reluctant to execute him outright.
units.literal: Your servant also knows that Yijing is a descendant of the Gaozong Chun Emperor, and the Emperor, cherishing kin and harmonizing the clan, is unwilling hastily to add manifest execution.

units.zh: 然即幸邀寬典，亦當禁錮終身，無為天潢宗室羞，豈圖收禁未及三月，輒复棄瑕錄用？
units.en: Even if he were spared, he should be imprisoned for life rather than bring shame on the imperial house—who imagined he would be released and reappointed in less than three months?
units.literal: Yet even if he fortunately receives lenient treatment, he should still be imprisoned for life, not bringing shame on the imperial clan—who would have thought that confinement had not reached three months before he was again employed despite his flaws?

units.zh: 且此數人者，皇上特未知其見惡於民之深耳。
units.en: Moreover, Your Majesty may not yet realize how deeply the people hate these men.
units.literal: Moreover, regarding these several men, the Emperor simply does not yet know how deeply they are hated by the people.

units.zh: 倘俯採輿論，孰不切齒琦善為罪魁，誰不疾首於奕山、奕經、牛鑑、文蔚，而以為投畀之不容緩？
units.en: If Your Majesty heeded public opinion, who would not denounce Qishan as the chief culprit, or demand that Yishan, Yijing, Niu Jian, and Wenwei be cast out without delay?
units.literal: If Your Majesty would condescend to adopt popular opinion, who would not gnash teeth at Qishan as chief culprit? Who would not wring hands at Yishan, Yijing, Niu Jian, and Wenwei, and regard casting them out as not to be delayed?

units.zh: 此非臣一人之私言也。
units.en: This is not my opinion alone.
units.literal: This is not your servant's private words alone.

units.zh: 側聞琦善意侈體汰，跋扈如常，葉爾羌之行，本屬怏怏；
units.en: I hear that Qishan remains as extravagant and overbearing as ever and went to Yarkand reluctantly;
units.literal: Your servant has heard on the side that Qishan's intentions were extravagant and his person dissolute, overbearing as before; the journey to Yarkand was originally undertaken resentfully;

units.zh: 今果未及出關，即蒙召還。
units.en: and before he had even left the frontier pass, he was recalled.
units.literal: now in truth before he had even passed beyond the pass he received summons to return.

units.zh: 熱河密邇神京，有識無識，莫不撫膺太息，以為皇上鄉用琦善之意，尚不止此。
units.en: Rehe lies close to the capital; learned and common people alike sigh in dismay, fearing the Emperor intends to employ Qishan even closer to court.
units.literal: Rehe is close to the divine capital; the informed and uninformed alike beat their breasts and sigh deeply, thinking the Emperor's intention to employ Qishan near home does not stop here.

units.zh: 萬一有事，則熒惑聖聰者，必仍系斯人。
units.en: If trouble should arise again, this same man would surely be the one to mislead Your Majesty.
units.literal: If by chance something occurs, then he who would bewilder the sage hearing must still be this man.

units.zh: 履霜堅冰，深可懍懼。
units.en: As the proverb says, frost underfoot foretells solid ice—a prospect that should fill us with dread.
units.literal: Treading frost leads to solid ice—deeply to be feared with dread.

units.zh: 頃者禦試翰詹，以'烹阿封即墨'命題，而今茲刑賞顧如此，臣未知皇上所謂阿者何人？
units.en: At the recent Hanlin examination the topic was "boiling A and enfeoffing Jimo," yet rewards and punishments now run the opposite way—I do not know whom Your Majesty considers "A."
units.literal: Recently at the imperial examination for Hanlin bachelors the topic was 'boiling A and enfeoffing Jimo'; yet now punishments and rewards turn out thus—your servant does not know whom the Emperor calls 'A'?

units.zh: 即墨者何人？
units.en: And who is "Jimo"?
units.literal: And who is 'Jimo'?

units.zh: 假如聖意高深，偶或差忒，而以即墨為阿，阿為即墨，將毋譽之毀之者有以淆亂是非耶？
units.en: If the imperial mind has erred and Jimo is treated as A and A as Jimo, will not flatterers and detractors alike confuse right and wrong?
units.literal: Suppose the sage intention is profound and occasionally errs, and Jimo is taken for A and A for Jimo—will not those who praise and those who destroy have means to confuse right and wrong?

units.zh: 所望皇上立奮天威，收回成命，體大學絜矩之旨，鑑盈廷毀譽之真，國法稍伸，民心可慰。」
units.en: I beg Your Majesty to rouse imperial authority, withdraw these appointments, heed the Great Learning's teaching on the measuring square, discern true praise and blame in the court, give the law some force, and console the people's hearts."
units.literal: What is hoped is that the Emperor will immediately rouse heavenly authority, withdraw the settled order, embody the Great Learning's intent of the measuring square, discern the truth of praise and blame filling the court, let state law be somewhat applied, and popular hearts be consoled.'

units.zh: 疏上，宣宗嘉之，諭曰：「朕無知人之明，以致琦善、奕經、文蔚諸人喪師失律，惟有反躬自責，不欲諉罪臣工。
units.en: When the memorial reached the throne, the Daoguang Emperor praised it and said: "I lacked the wisdom to judge men, and so Qishan, Yijing, Wenwei, and others lost armies and broke discipline. I can only blame myself and will not shift guilt onto my officials.
units.literal: When the memorial went up, the Xuanzong Emperor commended it and instructed, saying: 'We lack the clarity to know men, so that Qishan, Yijing, Wenwei, and the rest lost armies and violated discipline—we can only turn and blame ourselves, and do not wish to shift guilt onto officials.

units.zh: 今該御史請收回成命，朕非文過飾非之君，豈肯回護？」
units.en: This censor asks me to withdraw my orders. I am not a ruler who covers his faults—how could I shield them?"
units.literal: Now this censor requests withdrawing the settled order. We are not a ruler who covers faults and whitewashes errors—how could We be willing to shield them?'

units.zh: 复革琦善等職，令閉門思過。
units.en: He then stripped Qishan and the others of their posts and ordered them to remain at home in reflection.
units.literal: He again stripped Qishan and the others of office and ordered them to close their doors and reflect on their faults.

units.zh: 於是直聲震海內。
units.en: His reputation for integrity then resounded throughout the empire.
units.literal: Thereupon his upright reputation shook all within the seas.

units.zh: 二十五年，遷給事中，巡視東城，以事詿吏議，左遷光祿寺署正。
units.en: In Daoguang 25 he was made supervising secretary and inspector of the Eastern City, but was demoted to acting director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments after an official inquiry.
units.literal: In the twenty-fifth year he was transferred to supervising secretary, inspected the Eastern City, was implicated in an official matter in deliberation, and was demoted to acting director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments.

units.zh: 二十六年，乞歸。
units.en: In Daoguang 26 he asked leave to return home.
units.literal: In the twenty-sixth year he requested to return home.

units.zh: 文宗即位，以大學士朱鳳標薦，复授御史，蹶而再起，氣不少撓，疊上疏多關大計。
units.en: When the Xianfeng Emperor ascended, Grand Secretary Zhu Fengbiao recommended him for censor again; though he had fallen, he rose once more undaunted and submitted repeated memorials on matters of state.
units.literal: When the Wenzong Emperor ascended, on Grand Secretary Zhu Fengbiao's recommendation he was again appointed censor; though he stumbled, he rose again, his spirit not much bent, and repeatedly submitted memorials mostly concerning great policy.

units.zh: 自粵匪起，福建群盜蠢動，蔓延泉、漳、興、永諸郡。
units.en: After the Taiping rebellion began, bandit gangs stirred in Fujian and spread through Quanzhou, Zhangzhou, Xinghua, and Yongchun.
units.literal: Since the Cantonese rebels arose, bandit gangs in Fujian stirred, spreading through Quan, Zhang, Xing, Yong, and other prefectures.

units.zh: 咸豐三年，慶鏞疏陳利害，命回籍治團練。
units.en: In Xianfeng 3 he memorialized on the situation and was ordered home to organize local militia.
units.literal: In the third year of Xianfeng, Qingyong memorialized on advantages and harms and was ordered to return to his native place to organize militia training.

units.zh: 惠安妖婦邱氏煽亂，偵獲置諸法，賜花翎。
units.en: He detected and executed the sorceress Qiu, who had incited rebellion in Huian, and was rewarded with the peacock feather.
units.literal: The sorceress Qiu of Huian incited rebellion; detected and captured, she was punished by law, and he was granted the peacock feather.

units.zh: 俄以病請開缺。
units.en: He soon asked leave of his post on grounds of illness.
units.literal: Soon after, on grounds of illness he requested leave of his post.

units.zh: 七年，逆匪林俊糾莆陽、仙遊、永春、南安群賊犯泉州，慶鏞激厲士民固守，賊攻圍數日而退。
units.en: In Xianfeng 7 the rebel Lin Jun gathered bandits from Putian, Xianyou, Yongchun, and Nan'an to attack Quanzhou; Qingyong rallied the gentry and people to hold the city, and the rebels withdrew after several days.
units.literal: In the seventh year the rebel Lin Jun gathered bandits from Putian, Xianyou, Yongchun, and Nan'an to attack Quanzhou; Qingyong roused officials and people to hold firm, and after besieging for several days the bandits withdrew.

units.zh: 論功，以道員候選。
units.en: For this service he was made a candidate for circuit intendant.
units.literal: His merit was discussed and he was made a candidate for circuit intendant.

units.zh: 八年，卒於泉州，贈光祿寺卿，賜祭葬，廕一子知縣，祀鄉賢祠。
units.en: He died at Quanzhou in Xianfeng 8 and was posthumously made vice minister of the Court of Imperial Entertainments, granted state funeral honors, with one son ennobled as county magistrate and his spirit enshrined in the local worthies' temple.
units.literal: In the eighth year he died at Quanzhou; posthumously he was granted vice minister of the Court of Imperial Entertainments, granted sacrificial burial, one son was ennobled as county magistrate, and he was enshrined in the local worthies' temple.

units.zh: 慶鏞精研漢學​​，而製行則服膺宋儒，文辭樸茂，著有籀經堂文集、三家詩考、說文釋、古籀考等書。
units.en: Qingyong was a scholar of Han learning who followed Song Confucian conduct in life; his prose was plain and solid. He left the Zhoujing Hall Collected Works, Examination of the Three Schools' Poetry, Explanation of the Shuowen, Examination of Ancient Zhou Script, and other works.
units.literal: Qingyong deeply studied Han learning, yet in conduct he adhered to Song Confucians; his literary style was plain and rich; he authored the Zhoujing Hall Collected Works, Examination of the Three Schools' Poetry, Explanation of the Shuowen, Examination of Ancient Zhou Script, and other books.

units.zh: 蘇廷魁，字賡堂，廣東高要人。
units.en: Su Tingkui (style name Gengtang) came from Gaoyao in Guangdong.
units.literal: Su Tingkui, courtesy name Gengtang, was a man of Gaoyao in Guangdong.

units.zh: 道光十五年進士，選庶吉士，授編修。
units.en: He earned his jinshi in Daoguang 15 (1835), entered the Hanlin Academy, and was made a compiling editor.
units.literal: In the fifteenth year of Daoguang he became a jinshi, was selected as a Hanlin bachelor, and was appointed compiling editor.

units.zh: 二十二年，遷御史。
units.en: In Daoguang 22 he was made a censor.
units.literal: In the twenty-second year he was transferred to censor.

units.zh: 海疆兵事方亟，迭上疏論列，請修築虎門砲台及燕塘墟、大沙河、龜岡諸要隘，以防敵回擾粵，既而和議成。
units.en: As coastal war intensified, he repeatedly memorialized urging repair of the Humen batteries and the passes at Yantangxu, Dashaha, and Guigang to guard against a return attack on Guangdong—until peace was concluded.
units.literal: Coastal military affairs were then urgent; he repeatedly memorialized in discussion, requesting repair and construction of the Humen batteries and the strategic passes at Yantangxu, Dashaha, and Guigang to guard against the enemy returning to harass Guangdong—soon after peace was concluded.

units.zh: 二十三年春，有白氣自天西南隅直掃參旗，因災異上疏數千言，極論時政乖迕，歸罪樞臣穆彰阿等，請立罷黜；
units.en: In the spring of Daoguang 23 a white comet swept from the southwest through the Shen constellation; he submitted a memorial of several thousand words on this omen, condemning current policy and blaming Grand Councilor Mujangga and others, demanding their immediate dismissal;
units.literal: In the spring of the twenty-third year a white vapor from the southwestern corner of heaven swept straight through the Shen asterism; because of this omen he memorialized several thousand words, speaking at length on current policy's perversity, attributing guilt to Grand Councilor Mujangga and others, and requesting immediate dismissal;

units.zh: 並下罪己詔，開直諫之路：語多指斥。
units.en: and calling for an imperial self-reproach edict and open remonstrance—his language was blunt and accusatory.
units.literal: and also issuing an imperial self-reproach edict and opening the path of blunt remonstrance—the language contained much direct accusation.

units.zh: 宣宗覽奏動容，嘉其切直，朝野傾望丰采。
units.en: The Daoguang Emperor was moved by the memorial and praised its blunt honesty; court and public alike looked to him with admiration.
units.literal: The Xuanzong Emperor, reading the memorial, was moved; he commended its blunt directness, and court and populace looked to him with admiration.

units.zh: 遭憂去官，服闋，遷給事中。
units.en: After a period of mourning he was made supervising secretary.
units.literal: He entered mourning and left office; when mourning ended he was transferred to supervising secretary.

units.zh: 咸豐元年，上謹始疏，請求宏濟之道，執勞謙之義，防驕泰之萌，推誠任賢，慎始圖治，選擇翰詹為講官，嚴取孝廉方正備採用，文宗嘉納之。
units.en: In Xianfeng 1 he submitted a memorial on careful beginnings, urging policies of great relief, humility in labor, guarding against pride, sincerity in employing talent, careful governance at the start, Hanlin lecturers, and strict selection of filial and upright candidates—the Xianfeng Emperor accepted it with praise.
units.literal: In the first year of Xianfeng he submitted a memorial on being careful at the beginning, requesting the Way of great relief, holding to the principle of labor and humility, guarding against the sprouting of pride and ease, extending sincerity and employing the worthy, being careful at the start and planning good government, selecting Hanlin bachelors as lecturers, strictly selecting filial and incorrupt candidates for reserve employment—the Wenzong Emperor commended and accepted it.

units.zh: 賽尚阿出督師，援引內閣侍讀穆廕擢五品京堂，在軍機大臣上學習行走。
units.en: When Saišangga went out to command the army, he promoted Grand Secretariat reader Muyin to fifth-rank capital official and placed him to learn duties above the Grand Council.
units.literal: Saišangga went out to command the army and cited Grand Secretariat reader-in-waiting Muyin for promotion to fifth-rank capital official, learning duties above the Grand Councilors.

units.zh: 廷魁疏劾其壞舊制，用私親，超擢太驟，易啟幸進之門，請俟賽尚阿還，令回章京本任，詔斥擅預黜陟，猶以素行端方，不之罪。
units.en: Tingkui impeached this as a breach of precedent, nepotism, and reckless promotion that opened the door to favoritism, and asked that Muyin return to his clerk post when Saišangga came back. An edict rebuked Tingkui for interfering in appointments, but spared him because of his upright record.
units.literal: Tingkui memorialized impeaching him for damaging old institutions, employing private kin, promoting too hastily, easily opening the gate of favor-seeking advancement; he requested waiting until Saišangga returned and ordering him back to his original clerk post. An edict rebuked him for presumptuously interfering in dismissal and promotion, yet because his conduct had always been upright, he was not punished.

units.zh: 上先隱其名，出疏示賽尚阿，賽尚阿退，飲台垣酒，問：「誰實彈我？」
units.en: The Emperor first concealed Tingkui's name and showed the memorial to Saišangga; when Saišangga withdrew and drank with the censorial officials, he asked, "Who impeached me?"
units.literal: The Emperor first concealed his name and showed the memorial to Saišangga; Saišangga withdrew, drank wine with the censorial officials, and asked: 'Who really impeached me?'

units.zh: 廷魁出席曰：「公負國，某不敢負公。」
units.en: Tingkui rose and said, "You have failed the state; I dare not fail you by concealing it."
units.literal: Tingkui rose from his seat and said: 'You have failed the state; I dare not fail you.'

units.zh: 再以憂歸。
units.en: He again returned home to observe mourning.
units.literal: He again returned home on mourning.

units.zh: 四年，廣東紅巾匪起，將犯省城。
units.en: In Xianfeng 4 the Red Turban rebels rose in Guangdong and threatened the provincial capital.
units.literal: In the fourth year the Guangdong Red Turban bandits arose and were about to attack the provincial capital.

units.zh: 或獻議借外兵，以鋪捐為餉糈，力爭，罷其議。
units.en: Some proposed borrowing foreign troops and funding them with shop levies; he fought the proposal and had it dropped.
units.literal: Some offered the plan of borrowing foreign troops and using shop levies as army provisions; he strove against it and had the plan abolished.

units.zh: 八年，英法聯軍踞廣州，廷魁與侍郎羅惇衍等倡設團防局，嚴清野，絕漢奸，招募東莞及三元里、佛山練勇得數万人，聲言戒期攻城，敵師出，擊斬百餘級。
units.en: In Xianfeng 8 the Anglo-French forces occupied Guangzhou; Tingkui and Vice Minister Luo Dunyan organized a militia defense bureau, cleared the countryside, cut off collaborators, and recruited tens of thousands of militia from Dongguan, Sanyuanli, and Foshan; when they announced an attack and the enemy came out, they killed more than a hundred.
units.literal: In the eighth year the Anglo-French allied armies occupied Guangzhou; Tingkui together with Vice Minister Luo Dunyan and others initiated establishment of a militia defense bureau, strictly cleared the countryside, cut off Chinese traitors, recruited militia from Dongguan and Sanyuanli and Foshan numbering tens of thousands, announced a set day to attack the city; when enemy troops came out, they struck and beheaded more than a hundred.

units.zh: 敵始有戒心，稍戢，連艘北犯，既而天津議和，廣東敵兵未退，民益憤，廷魁等請留練局以防土寇。
units.en: The enemy grew cautious and withdrew somewhat, then sailed north; after peace at Tianjin the foreign troops remained in Guangdong and popular anger grew; Tingkui asked to keep the militia bureau against local bandits.
units.literal: The enemy first grew cautious and somewhat restrained, then sent ships in succession north to invade; soon after peace was negotiated at Tianjin, yet Guangdong enemy troops had not withdrawn and the people grew angrier; Tingkui and others requested keeping the militia bureau to guard against local bandits.

units.zh: 敵謂既媾和何復募勇，且以懸金購領事巴夏禮為責言。
units.en: The foreigners protested that recruiting militia after peace was improper and blamed the Chinese for posting a bounty on Consul Harry Parkes.
units.literal: The enemy said that since peace had been made, why recruit militia again, and also blamed them for posting a reward to buy Consul Parkes.

units.zh: 議和大臣桂良慮撓成議，奏請撤局。
units.en: Peace negotiator Guiliang feared this would disrupt the treaty and memorialized to dissolve the bureau.
units.literal: Peace negotiator Guiliang feared disturbing the concluded agreement and memorialized requesting dissolution of the bureau.

units.zh: 初，艇匪擾廣寧，圍四會、肇慶，兵疲糧罄，或勸之去，廷魁曰：「予團防大臣也，誓與城為存亡！」
units.en: Earlier, when boat bandits besieged Sihui and Zhaoqing in Guangning and troops were exhausted, some urged him to flee. Tingkui said, "I am the militia defense commissioner—I swear to live or die with this city!"
units.literal: Earlier, boat bandits harassed Guangning and besieged Sihui and Zhaoqing; troops were weary and grain exhausted; some urged him to leave. Tingkui said: 'I am the militia defense commissioner—I swear to live and die with the city!'

units.zh: 會提督昆壽克梧州，以兵來援，城得完。
units.en: Provincial Commander Kunshou then captured Wuzhou and came to the rescue, and the city was saved.
units.literal: It happened that Provincial Commander Kunshou captured Wuzhou and came with troops to relieve; the city was preserved intact.

units.zh: 疆臣屢欲上其功，皆固辭。
units.en: Frontier officials repeatedly tried to memorialize his merits, but he firmly declined.
units.literal: Frontier officials repeatedly wished to memorialize his merit; he firmly declined all.

units.zh: 同治初，以中外大臣薦，授河南開歸陳許道，歷布政使，擢東河總督。
units.en: Early in the Tongzhi reign, on ministers' recommendation, he was made intendant of the Kai-Gui-Chen-Xu circuit in Henan, served as provincial treasurer, and was promoted to Governor-General of the Eastern Rivers.
units.literal: At the beginning of Tongzhi, on recommendation of capital and provincial ministers, he was appointed intendant of the Kai-Gui-Chen-Xu circuit in Henan, served as provincial treasurer, and was promoted to Governor-General of the Eastern Rivers.

units.zh: 七年，河決滎澤，未奪溜，革職留任，閱三月工竣，復之。
units.en: In Tongzhi 7 the Yellow River breached at Xingze without shifting course; he was dismissed but kept in post, and after three months' work was restored.
units.literal: In the seventh year the Yellow River broke at Xingze without shifting its course; he was stripped of office but retained in post; after three months the work was completed and he was restored.

units.zh: 逾年，內召，去官，稱疾歸。
units.en: The following year he was summoned to the capital, resigned, and returned home on grounds of illness.
units.literal: After more than a year he was summoned to the capital, left office, and returned home claiming illness.

units.zh: 光緒四年，卒。
units.en: He died in Guangxu 4 (1878).
units.literal: In the fourth year of Guangxu he died.

units.zh: 朱琦，字伯韓，廣西臨桂人。
units.en: Zhu Qi (style name Bohan) came from Lingui in Guangxi.
units.literal: Zhu Qi, courtesy name Bohan, was a man of Lingui in Guangxi.

units.zh: 父鳳森，嘉慶六年進士，官河南濬縣知縣，有政聲。
units.en: His father Zhu Fengsen earned his jinshi in Jiaqing 6 (1801), served as magistrate of Jun County in Henan, and won a reputation for good governance.
units.literal: His father Fengsen became a jinshi in the sixth year of Jiaqing, served as magistrate of Jun County in Henan, and had a reputation for good governance.

units.zh: 滑縣教匪起，率團練御之，屢破賊，城守卒完。
units.en: When sectarian rebels rose in Hua County, he led the militia in repeated victories and preserved the city.
units.literal: When sectarian rebels arose in Hua County, he led militia to resist them, repeatedly defeated the bandits, and the city defense was finally preserved intact.

units.zh: 遷河南府通判。
units.en: He was promoted to vice prefect of Henan Prefecture.
units.literal: He was transferred to vice prefect of Henan Prefecture.

units.zh: 歿，祀名宦。
units.en: After his death he was enshrined among distinguished officials.
units.literal: When he died he was enshrined among famous officials.

units.zh: 琦，舉鄉試第一。
units.en: Zhu Qi placed first in the provincial examinations.
units.literal: Qi placed first in the provincial examination.

units.zh: 道光十五年，成進士，選庶吉士，授編修。
units.en: He earned his jinshi in Daoguang 15 (1835), entered the Hanlin Academy, and was made a compiling editor.
units.literal: In the fifteenth year of Daoguang he became a jinshi, was selected as a Hanlin bachelor, and was appointed compiling editor.

units.zh: 慕同里陳宏謀之為人，以氣節自勵。
units.en: He admired the character of his fellow townsman Chen Hongmou and strove to live by moral integrity.
units.literal: He admired the conduct of his fellow townsman Chen Hongmou and encouraged himself with integrity of spirit.

units.zh: 遷御史，值海疆事定，禍機四伏，而上下復習委靡，言路多容默，深以為憂。
units.en: Made a censor after the coastal war ended, he saw danger lurking everywhere while court and country relapsed into listlessness and the censorate fell silent—he was deeply troubled.
units.literal: He was transferred to censor; it happened that coastal affairs were settled, yet peril lurked on four sides, while above and below again practiced listlessness; the avenue of speech was mostly tolerant silence—he was deeply worried.

units.zh: 著名實說，略曰：「天下有鄉曲之行，有大人之行。
units.en: He wrote a treatise On Reputation and Reality, opening: "Under Heaven there is the conduct of petty localism and the conduct of great statesmen.
units.literal: He wrote a treatise on reputation and reality, in summary saying: 'Under Heaven there is the conduct of village lanes and there is the conduct of great men.

units.zh: 鄉曲、大人，其名也，考之其行，而察其有用與否，其實也。
units.en: Petty localism and great statesmanship are only names; examine conduct and whether it serves the state--that is reality.
units.literal: 'Village lanes' and 'great men' are names; examine their conduct and observe whether they are useful or not—that is the reality.

units.zh: 世之稱者，曰謹厚，曰廉靜，日退讓，三者名之至美也，而不知此鄉曲之行也，非所謂大人者也。
units.en: The age praises "prudent and solid," "pure and quiet," and "daily yielding"—names of the highest beauty—yet these are petty conduct, not the conduct of great statesmen.
units.literal: What the age praises are called 'prudent and solid,' 'pure and quiet,' and 'daily yielding'—these three names are the most beautiful, yet one does not know that this is the conduct of village lanes, not what is called great men.

units.zh: 大人之職，在於經國家、安社稷，有剛毅之大節，為人主畏憚；
units.en: The duty of great statesmen is to govern the state and secure the realm: they possess firm integrity and are feared and respected by the sovereign;
units.literal: The duty of great men lies in ordering the state and securing the altars of soil and grain; they have great integrity of firm resolution and are feared and respected by the ruler;

units.zh: 有深謀遠慮，為天下長計。
units.en: they plan deeply and far ahead for the empire's lasting good.
units.literal: they have deep plans and far-reaching thought and make long-term plans for all under Heaven.

units.zh: 合則留，不合以義去。
units.en: If their counsel is heeded they stay; if not, they leave on principle.
units.literal: If in accord they stay; if not in accord they leave on grounds of righteousness.

units.zh: 身之便安，不暇計也；
units.en: They do not calculate their personal comfort;
units.literal: Personal ease and comfort—they have no leisure to calculate;

units.zh: 世之指摘，不敢逃也。
units.en: nor do they flee the world's blame.
units.literal: the age's finger-pointing—they dare not flee.

units.zh: 今也不然。
units.en: Now it is otherwise.
units.literal: Now it is not so.

units.zh: 曰：吾為天下長計，則天下之釁必集於我；
units.en: They say: if I plan for the empire's long-term good, the world's troubles will fall on me;
units.literal: They say: If I make long-term plans for all under Heaven, then the world's troubles will surely gather on me;

units.zh: 吾為人主畏憚，則不能久於其位；
units.en: if I am feared and respected by the sovereign, I cannot long keep my post;
units.literal: if I am feared and respected by the ruler, then I cannot long remain in my post;

units.zh: 不如謹厚、廉靜、退讓，此三者可以安坐而無患，而名又至美也。
units.en: better to be prudent, pure, and yielding—one can sit secure without trouble and win the fairest name.
units.literal: better to be prudent and solid, pure and quiet, and yielding—these three allow one to sit securely without worry, and the name is again most beautiful.

units.zh: 夫無患而可久於其位，又有天下美名，士何憚而不爭趨於此？
units.en: What gentleman would not strive for a post without worry, long tenure, and a beautiful reputation?
units.literal: Now, without worry and able to long remain in one's post, and also having the world's beautiful name—what would gentlemen fear that they would not all strive toward this?

units.zh: 故近世所稱公卿之賢者，此三者為多矣。
units.en: Hence most of the "worthy" ministers praised in recent times excel in these three qualities alone.
units.literal: Therefore among the worthy high ministers praised in recent times, these three are the most numerous.

units.zh: 當其瓘冠襜裾，從容正步，趨於廊廟之間，上之人不疑，而非議不加，其沉深不可測也。
units.en: In jade caps and court robes they walk with easy dignity through the palace corridors; their superiors trust them and no one criticizes them—they seem unfathomably deep.
units.literal: When they wear jade caps and long robes, walk with easy, proper steps, and hasten between palace corridors, their superiors do not doubt them and no censure is added—their depth cannot be fathomed.

units.zh: 一旦遇大利害，搶攘無措，鉗口撟舌而莫敢言，而所謂謹厚、廉靜、退讓，至此舉無可用，於是始思向之為人主畏憚而有深謀遠慮者，不可得矣。
units.en: Yet when great crisis comes they are helpless, silent and tongue-tied—and their prudence, purity, and yielding prove wholly useless; only then do they realize that the statesmen once feared and respected by the sovereign, with deep vision, are nowhere to be found.
units.literal: Once they encounter great advantage and harm, they are flustered without resource, clamp their mouths and twist their tongues and dare not speak—and the so-called prudent, pure, and yielding qualities are at this point wholly useless; only then do they begin to think of those formerly feared by the ruler and with deep plans and far-reaching thought, but they cannot be obtained.

units.zh: 且謹厚、廉靜、退讓三者，非果無用也。
units.en: Yet prudence, purity, and yielding are not in themselves useless.
units.literal: Moreover, the three qualities of prudence, purity, and yielding are not in truth useless.

units.zh: 古有負蓋世之功而思持其後，挾震主之威而唯恐不終，未嘗不斤斤於此，故又於鎮薄俗、保晚節。
units.en: Ancient men who had achieved world-shaking merit and sought to preserve it, or who wielded power that awed the throne and feared an unhappy end, were scrupulous in these virtues to restrain shallow custom and preserve their integrity in old age.
units.literal: In antiquity those who bore world-surpassing merit and thought to sustain it afterward, or who wielded authority that awed the ruler and feared they would not finish—none failed to be scrupulous in these matters; therefore they also used them to restrain shallow customs and preserve integrity in later years.

units.zh: 後世無其才而冒其位，安其樂而避其患，假於名之至美，僴然自以為足。
units.en: Later men without such talent hold such posts, enjoy their ease while avoiding trouble, borrow these fairest names, and complacently think themselves sufficient.
units.literal: Later generations, without such talent yet usurping such posts, secure in their pleasure and avoiding their troubles, borrow the most beautiful names and complacently think themselves sufficient.

units.zh: 是藏身之固，莫便此三者。
units.en: Nothing offers a safer hiding place than these three virtues.
units.literal: This is the firmest hiding-place—nothing is more convenient than these three.

units.zh: 孔子之所謂鄙夫也，其究鄉愿也。
units.en: They are what Confucius called vulgar men—in the end, village worthies in disguise.
units.literal: They are what Confucius called vulgar fellows; in the end they are village worthies.

units.zh: 是張禹、胡廣、趙戒之類也，甚矣其恥也！」
units.en: They are men of the sort of Zhang Yu, Hu Guang, and Zhao Jie—how shameful!"
units.literal: They are the sort of Zhang Yu, Hu Guang, and Zhao Jie—how great their shame!'

units.zh: 於是數上疏切論時務，皆留中不報。
units.en: He then submitted repeated memorials on urgent affairs of state, but all were retained at court without response.
units.literal: Thereupon he repeatedly submitted memorials bluntly discussing current affairs; all were retained at court without response.

units.zh: 時咸推其抗直，稱為名御史。
units.en: His contemporaries admired his outspoken integrity and called him a censor of renown.
units.literal: At the time all praised his resistance and bluntness and called him a famous censor.

units.zh: 琦以言既不見用，二十六年，告歸。
units.en: When his counsel went unheeded, he asked leave to return home in Daoguang 26.
units.literal: Because Qi's words were not employed, in the twenty-sixth year he requested to return home.

units.zh: 越數年，廣西群賊蜂起，其言皆驗。
units.en: Within a few years bandits swarmed in Guangxi, and his warnings proved true.
units.literal: After several years bandit gangs in Guangxi swarmed like bees; all his words were verified.

units.zh: 家居治團練，助守禦。
units.en: At home he organized local militia and helped defend the region.
units.literal: At home he organized militia training and assisted in defense.

units.zh: 賊中梟傑張家祥者，悔罪投誠，當事猶疑之。
units.en: The rebel chieftain Zhang Jiaxiang repented and offered to surrender, but the authorities still distrusted him.
units.literal: Among the bandits the chieftain Zhang Jiaxiang repented his crimes and submitted in good faith; the authorities still doubted him.

units.zh: 琦知其忠勇可用，以全家保之，乃受降，改名國樑，卒為名將。
units.en: Qi judged him loyal and brave enough to use, pledged his own family's safety as guarantee, accepted the surrender, renamed him Guoliang, and he became a famous general.
units.literal: Qi knew his loyalty and courage could be employed, guaranteed him with his whole family, then accepted his surrender; he changed his name to Guoliang and in the end became a famous general.

units.zh: 琦以守城勞議敘，以道員候選。
units.en: For his service in the city's defense he was made a candidate for circuit intendant.
units.literal: Qi's merit in defending the city was discussed for reward; he was made a candidate for circuit intendant.

units.zh: 咸豐六年，再至京師。
units.en: In Xianfeng 6 he returned to Beijing.
units.literal: In the sixth year of Xianfeng he again reached the capital.

units.zh: 居兩歲，從欽差大臣桂良至江蘇，無所遇，王有齡獨重之，有齡撫浙，闢贊軍事。
units.en: After two years he followed Imperial Commissioner Guiliang to Jiangsu without success until Wang Youling alone valued him; when Wang became governor of Zhejiang, he recruited Qi to assist in military affairs.
units.literal: After residing two years he followed Imperial Commissioner Guiliang to Jiangsu, met with no success; Wang Youling alone valued him—when Youling became governor of Zhejiang, he recruited him to assist in military affairs.

units.zh: 十一年，粵匪犯杭州，總理團練局。
units.en: In Xianfeng 11 the Taiping rebels attacked Hangzhou, and he directed the militia bureau.
units.literal: In the eleventh year the Cantonese rebels attacked Hangzhou; he directed the militia training bureau.

units.zh: 守清波門，城陷，死之。
units.en: He defended the Qingbo Gate; when the city fell, he died in its defense.
units.literal: He defended the Qingbo Gate; the city fell and he died.

units.zh: 贈太常寺卿，予騎都尉世職，祀昭忠祠。
units.en: He was posthumously made vice minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, granted a hereditary commandant of cavalry rank, and enshrined in the Shrine of Manifest Loyalty.
units.literal: Posthumously he was granted vice minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, given the hereditary office of commandant of cavalry, and enshrined in the Shrine of Manifest Loyalty.

units.zh: 琦學宗程、朱，詩古文皆有法，著有怡志堂集、台垣奏議。
units.en: Qi followed the Cheng-Zhu school of Neo-Confucianism; his poetry and prose were disciplined in style. He left the Yizhi Hall Collected Works and Censorial Memorials.
units.literal: Qi's learning followed the Cheng and Zhu school; his poetry and ancient prose all had method; he authored the Yizhi Hall Collected Works and Censorial Memorials.

units.zh: 論曰：禁煙之議，創自黃爵滋，行之操切，而邊釁遂開，繼之游移而國威愈墮，誠不可以此歸咎始議之人。
units.en: The historian comments: Huang Juezi originated the proposal to ban opium. It was enforced with harsh urgency, border war followed, and vacillation afterward only further diminished national prestige—yet the blame cannot fairly be laid on those who first proposed the ban.
units.literal: The commentator says: The proposal to ban opium was initiated by Huang Juezi; carried out with harsh urgency, border hostilities thereupon opened; what followed was vacillation and national prestige fell ever lower—truly one cannot on this account blame those who first proposed the policy.

units.zh: 然謀國萬全，決胜千里，非恃意氣為也。
units.en: Yet securing the state and deciding victory a thousand li away cannot rest on zeal alone.
units.literal: Yet to plan for the state's complete security and decide victory a thousand li away cannot rely on high spirits alone.

units.zh: 行固維艱，言亦豈易易哉？
units.en: Action is hard enough—how much harder is it to speak rightly?
units.literal: Action is indeed hard to sustain—how could speech be easy?

units.zh: 金應麟同被拔擢，亦始終主戰。
units.en: Jin Yinglin was promoted at the same time and likewise consistently favored war.
units.literal: Jin Yinglin was likewise specially promoted and also consistently advocated war.

units.zh: 陳慶鏞、蘇廷魁、朱琦時稱「三直」；
units.en: Chen Qingyong, Su Tingkui, and Zhu Qi were known as the "Three Upright Ones";
units.literal: Chen Qingyong, Su Tingkui, and Zhu Qi were at the time called 'the Three Upright';

units.zh: 合之應麟，又稱「四虎」。
units.en: with Yinglin added, they were called the "Four Tigers."
units.literal: adding Yinglin, they were again called 'the Four Tigers.'

units.zh: 所言有用有不用，凜凜然有生氣，要足以砭頑振懦矣。
units.en: Their counsel was sometimes heeded and sometimes ignored, yet they spoke with stern moral force enough to pierce stubbornness and rouse the timid.
units.literal: What they said was sometimes employed and sometimes not; stern and awe-inspiring, they had living spirit—enough in essence to pierce the stubborn and rouse the timid.

units.zh: 咸豐四年，科爾沁親王僧格林沁剿捻，檄取察哈爾戰馬六百匹，不堪乘用，奏聞。
units.en: Xianfeng 4 (1854) Prince Senggelinqin of Horqin, fighting the Nian, requisitioned 600 Chakhar war horses—they proved unrideable, and he reported it.
units.literal: In the fourth year of Xianfeng Prince Senggelinqin of Horqin, suppressing the Nian rebels, requisitioned six hundred Chakhar war horses; they were unfit for riding, and this was reported.

units.zh: 上大怒，嚴諭都統慶昀整頓，蓋馬政漸衰弛矣。
units.en: The emperor was furious and ordered banner commander Qing Yun to set things right—horse administration was clearly in decline.
units.literal: The emperor was greatly angered and sternly ordered banner commander Qing Yun to rectify matters—for horse administration was gradually declining.

units.zh: 咸豐初，哲布尊丹巴等捐馬千匹，喀爾喀土謝圖等二千匹，錫林果勒盟長等三千匹，帝以其多，卻之。
units.en: Early in Xianfeng, Jebtsundamba donated 1,000 horses, Khalkha Tushiyetu 2,000, and Xilin Gol league chiefs 3,000—the emperor declined them as excessive.
units.literal: Early in Xianfeng Jebtsundamba and others donated one thousand horses, Khalkha Tushiyetu two thousand, Xilin Gol league chiefs three thousand; the emperor, because they were too many, declined them.

units.zh: 嗣聞已在途中，令擇善地牧以待用。
units.en: Learning they were already en route, he ordered good pasture found to hold them until needed.
units.literal: Later learning they were already on the road, he ordered good pasture chosen to hold them until use.

units.zh: 尚書敬顯儁曰：「孔子云：『微管仲，吾其被發左衽矣』以此言之，右衽為是。」
units.en: Minister Jing Xianjun said, "Confucius said, 'Were it not for Guan Zhong, we would wear our hair loose and our lapel to the left.' By this reasoning the right lapel is correct."
units.literal: Minister Jing Xianjun said, "Confucius said, 'Were it not for Guan Zhong, we would wear our hair loose and our lapel to the left.' By this reasoning the right lapel is correct."

units.zh: 林則徐既罷，琦善主撫，復不得要領。
units.en: Lin Zexu had been dismissed; Qishan favored appeasement yet again failed to grasp essentials.
units.literal: Lin Zexu had already been dismissed; Qishan favored appeasement yet again failed to grasp essentials.

units.zh: 咸豐元年，奕山等以伊犁及烏魯木齊二處滿洲營增練鳥槍，擬定考驗章程，並綠營一律辦理。
units.en: In Xianfeng 1 Yishan added musket drill for Ili and Urumqi Manchu garrisons, set examination rules, and extended them to the Green Standard.
units.literal: In the first year of Xianfeng, Yishan and others, for Manchu camps at Ili and Urumqi, increased musket training, drafted examination regulations, and applied the same to Green Standard troops uniformly.

units.zh: 時林則徐為按察使，治海防，甚倚之。
units.en: At that time Lin Zexu was provincial judge overseeing coastal defense and relied on him heavily.
units.literal: At that time Lin Zexu was provincial judge and managed coastal defense; he relied on him greatly.

units.zh: 孫篤，道光二年進士，歷編修、御史，出為汀州知府、廣東督糧道，署鹽運使。
