units.en: His grandson Du, a jinshi in 1822, served as compiler, censor, prefect of Tingzhou, Guangdong grain superintendent, and acting salt controller.
units.literal: His grandson Du, a jinshi in the second year of Daoguang, served successively as compiler, censor, prefect of Tingzhou, grain superintendent of Guangdong, and acting salt controller.

units.zh: 咸豐元年，從大學士賽尚阿勦賊廣西，破紫金山西南砲台。
units.en: In 1851 he followed Grand Secretary Saishang'a to suppress rebels in Guangxi and captured the southwest battery on Zijin Mountain.
units.literal: In the first year of Xianfeng he followed Grand Secretary Saishang'a to suppress rebels in Guangxi and captured the southwest battery on Zijin Mountain.

units.zh: 及道光季年，張國樑募廣東潮州鄉兵追逐粵寇，轉戰東下，卒以獷悍不馴，遂至潰散。
units.en: Near the end of the Daoguang reign, Zhang Guoliang raised Chaozhou militia from Guangdong to chase the Cantonese rebels eastward, but their ferocity proved impossible to control, and the force eventually collapsed and scattered.
units.literal: By the late Daoguang period, Zhang Guoliang recruited local militia from Chaozhou, Guangdong, to pursue the Cantonese rebels, fighting eastward as they went; ultimately, because they were fierce and unruly, they broke up and dispersed.

units.zh: 程庭桂九月己酉乞養。十一月辛未羅惇衍左副都御史。
units.en: On the jiyou day of the ninth month, Cheng Tinggui requested leave to care for a parent. On the xinwei day of the eleventh month, Luo Dunyan: Left Deputy Censor-in-Chief.
units.literal: On the jiyou day of the ninth month, Cheng Tinggui requested leave to care for a parent. On the xinwei day of the eleventh month, Luo Dunyan: Left Deputy Censor-in-Chief.

units.zh: 咸豐二年壬子
units.en: Second year of Xianfeng (1852), renzi
units.literal: Second year of Xianfeng, renzi

units.zh: 羅惇衍二月甲申遷。雷以誠左副都御史。五月辛酉遷。周祖培左副都御史。十一月己酉遷。十二月乙酉龔文齡左副都御史。丙申遷。
units.en: On the jiashen day of the second month, Luo Dunyan was transferred. Lei Yicheng: Left Deputy Censor-in-Chief. On the xinyou day of the fifth month, was transferred. Zhou Zupei: Left Deputy Censor-in-Chief. On the jiyou day of the eleventh month, was transferred. On the yiyou day of the twelfth month, Gong Wenling: Left Deputy Censor-in-Chief. On the bingshen day, was transferred.
units.literal: On the jiashen day of the second month, Luo Dunyan was transferred. Lei Yicheng: Left Deputy Censor-in-Chief. On the xinyou day of the fifth month, was transferred. Zhou Zupei: Left Deputy Censor-in-Chief. On the jiyou day of the eleventh month, was transferred. On the yiyou day of the twelfth month, Gong Wenling: Left Deputy Censor-in-Chief. On the bingshen day, was transferred.

units.zh: 咸豐三年癸丑
units.en: Third year of Xianfeng (1853), guichou
units.literal: Third year of Xianfeng, guichou

units.zh: 萬青藜十月癸亥遷。甲子王慶雲左都御史。十二月庚午遷。羅惇衍左都御史。
units.en: On the guihai day of the tenth month, Wan Qingli was transferred. On the jiazi day, Wang Qingyun: Left Censor-in-Chief. On the gengwu day of the twelfth month, was transferred. Luo Dunyan: Left Censor-in-Chief.
units.literal: On the guihai day of the tenth month, Wan Qingli was transferred. On the jiazi day, Wang Qingyun: Left Censor-in-Chief. On the gengwu day of the twelfth month, was transferred. Luo Dunyan: Left Censor-in-Chief.

units.zh: 咸豐十一年辛酉
units.en: Eleventh year of Xianfeng (1861), xinyou
units.literal: Eleventh year of Xianfeng, xinyou

units.zh: 及論功當封，太尉胡廣時錄尚書事，承旨奏黜撫，天下怨之。
units.en: When honors were due for his victories, Grand Commandant Hu Guang—then directing the Secretariat—carried out an order to strip Teng Fu of recognition, and public opinion turned bitterly against the court.
units.literal: When merit was discussed and he ought to have been enfeoffed, Grand Commandant Hu Guang at the time held the office of recording imperial secretary affairs; receiving intent he memorialized to dismiss Fu—the realm resented it.

units.zh: 道光九年，回疆敉定，上太后徽號，緬甸國王遣使進金葉表，創舉也。
units.en: In the ninth year of Daoguang, after the Muslim frontier was pacified and honorific titles were conferred upon the empress dowager, the king of Burma sent envoys presenting a memorial on gold leaf—a first.
units.literal: In the ninth year of Daoguang, after the Muslim frontier was pacified and honorific titles were conferred upon the empress dowager, the king of Burma sent envoys presenting a memorial on gold leaf—a first.

units.zh: 故事，琉球間歲一貢，至十九年，詔改四年為期。
units.en: By precedent, Ryukyu paid tribute every other year; in the nineteenth year an edict changed the interval to four years.
units.literal: By precedent, Ryukyu paid tribute every other year; in the nineteenth year an edict changed the interval to four years.

units.zh: 報可。
units.en: The request was approved.
units.literal: The report was approved.

units.zh: 二十四年，湘潭民與江西客民閧，相殺傷，巡撫吳邦慶亦籍江西，陳奏偏袒。
units.en: In the twenty-fourth year locals in Xiangtan clashed with migrant settlers from Jiangxi, leaving casualties; Governor Wu Bangqing, himself a Jiangxi native, memorialized in a way that favored his fellow provincials.
units.literal: In the twenty-fourth year natives of Xiangtan and migrant settlers from Jiangxi clashed and killed and wounded one another; Governor Wu Bangqing, who was also a native of Jiangxi, memorialized in partial favor of his fellow provincials.

units.zh: 系英詢齎奏人，得事始末，於召對時面陳，乃調邦慶福建，詔以獄事畀總督察治。
units.en: Xiying questioned the memorial bearer and learned the full story; at an imperial audience he laid it out in person, and Bangqing was transferred to Fujian while the case was assigned to the governor-general for investigation.
units.literal: Xiying questioned the memorial bearer and learned how the affair began and ended; at an imperial audience he stated it in person, whereupon Bangqing was transferred to Fujian and an edict assigned the case to the governor-general for investigation.

units.zh: 系英素以樸直被眷遇，邦慶初與善，約地方事有見聞必告，至是手書言其曲直；
units.en: Xiying had long been favored for his plain integrity; Bangqing had been friendly with him and had agreed to keep him informed of local affairs, and now wrote in his own hand about the rights and wrongs of the case;
units.literal: Xiying had long been favored for his plain integrity; Bangqing had been on good terms with him at first and agreed that whatever he learned of local affairs he would report, and now wrote in his own hand about right and wrong in the case;

units.zh: 系英子汝楨亦致書在籍給事中石承藻詢獄事：書並為邦慶得，先後以兩書上聞。
units.en: Xiying's son Ruzhen also wrote the retired supervising secretary Shi Chengzao to inquire about the case; Bangqing obtained both letters and reported them to the throne in succession.
units.literal: Xiying's son Ruzhen also wrote to the retired supervising secretary Shi Chengzao to inquire about the case; both letters fell into Bangqing's hands and were reported to the throne in succession.

units.zh: 總督鄧廷楨已嚴申禁令，捕拏煙犯，洋商查頓先避回國。
units.en: Governor-General Deng Tingzhen had already tightened enforcement of the ban and arrested opium offenders; the merchant Jardine had already fled home.
units.literal: Governor-General Deng Tingzhen had already strictly proclaimed the prohibition, arrested opium offenders, and the foreign merchant Dent had already fled back to his country.

units.zh: 鄧廷楨，字嶰筠，江蘇江寧人。
units.en: Deng Tingzhen, styled Xiejun, was a native of Jiangning in Jiangsu.
units.literal: Deng Tingzhen, style name Xiejun, was a native of Jiangning in Jiangsu.

units.zh: 廷楨乃立限，責成保長，逾限及私造者置之法。
units.en: Deng set a deadline, held baojia heads responsible for compliance, and punished anyone who missed it or manufactured weapons in secret.
units.literal: Deng then set a deadline, held baojia heads responsible, and punished those who exceeded the deadline or manufactured weapons privately.

units.zh: 十五年，擢兩廣總督。
units.en: In 1835 he was promoted to governor-general of the Two Guang.
units.literal: In the fifteenth year he was promoted to Governor-General of the Two Guang.

units.zh: 嘉慶六年進士，選庶吉士，授編修。
units.en: In 1801 he passed the palace examination, entered the Hanlin Academy as a bachelor, and was appointed a compiler.
units.literal: In the sixth year of Jiaqing he became a jinshi, was selected as a Bachelor of the Hanlin Academy, and was appointed Compiler.

units.zh: 績學好士，幕府多名流，論學不輟。
units.en: A scholar himself, he loved to gather men of learning; his staff included many distinguished figures, and he never stopped discussing scholarship.
units.literal: He was deeply learned and loved scholars; his staff included many eminent men, and he never ceased discussing learning.

units.zh: 尤精於音韻之學，所著筆記、詩、詞並行世。
units.en: He was especially expert in phonology, and his notebooks, poetry, and song lyrics all circulated widely.
units.literal: He was especially skilled in phonology; his notebooks, poetry, and song lyrics all circulated in the world.

units.zh: 十五年，授台灣遺缺知府，浙江巡撫蔣攸銛請留浙，補寧波。
units.en: In 1810 he was appointed prefect to fill a vacancy in Taiwan, but Governor Jiang Youqian of Zhejiang asked that he remain in the province, and he was posted to Ningbo.
units.literal: In the fifteenth year he was appointed Prefect to fill a vacancy in Taiwan; Governor of Zhejiang Jiang Youqian requested that he remain in Zhejiang and he was appointed to Ningbo.

units.zh: 母憂歸，服闋，補陝西延安府，歷榆林、西安，以善折獄稱。
units.en: After mourning his mother he was assigned to Yan'an Prefecture in Shaanxi, later served in Yulin and Xi'an, and won renown for his skill in adjudicating cases.
units.literal: He returned home for his mother's mourning; when mourning ended he was appointed to Yan'an Prefecture in Shaanxi, served in Yulin and Xi'an, and was known for skill in resolving legal cases.

units.zh: 平反韓城、南鄭冤獄，又全同州嫠婦母子，陝民歌頌，傳播京師。
units.en: He overturned wrongful convictions in Hancheng and Nanzheng and saved a widow and her son in Tongzhou from injustice. The people of Shaanxi praised him, and word of his deeds reached the capital.
units.literal: He reversed wrongful convictions in Hancheng and Nanzheng, and also preserved the lives of a widow and her son in Tongzhou; the people of Shaanxi sang his praises, and the story spread to the capital.

units.zh: 二十五年，超擢湖北按察使，權布政使。
units.en: In 1820 he was promoted ahead of schedule to judicial commissioner of Hubei and acted as financial commissioner.
units.literal: In the twenty-fifth year he was promoted by special selection to Judicial Commissioner of Hubei and served as acting Financial Commissioner.

units.zh: 道光元年，遷江西布政使。
units.en: In 1821 he was transferred to financial commissioner of Jiangxi.
units.literal: In the first year of Daoguang he was transferred to Financial Commissioner of Jiangxi.

units.zh: 以前在西安失察渭南令故出縣民柳全璧殺人罪，罣誤，奪職。
units.en: He was stripped of office for having failed, while serving in Xi'an, to detect that the magistrate of Weinan had improperly released a county man named Liu Quanbi from a murder charge.
units.literal: Because while in Xi'an he had failed to detect that the magistrate of Weinan had improperly released the county man Liu Quanbi from a murder charge, he was implicated in error and dismissed from office.

units.zh: 議戍軍台，宣宗知其無私，特免遣戍，予七品銜，發直隸委用。
units.en: Although exile to a garrison post was proposed, Emperor Xuanzong knew he had acted without private motive and specially exempted him from banishment, gave him seventh-rank status, and assigned him to service in Zhili.
units.literal: It was proposed that he be sent to garrison duty; Emperor Xuanzong knew he had no private guilt and specially exempted him from exile, granted him seventh-rank status, and assigned him for service in Zhili.

units.zh: 尋授通永道。
units.en: He was soon appointed intendant of the Tongyong Circuit.
units.literal: Soon afterward he was appointed to the Tongyong Circuit.

units.zh: 四年，擢陝西按察使，遷布政使。
units.en: In 1824 he was promoted to judicial commissioner of Shaanxi and then to financial commissioner.
units.literal: In the fourth year he was promoted to Judicial Commissioner of Shaanxi and transferred to Financial Commissioner.

units.zh: 六年，擢安徽巡撫。
units.en: In 1826 he was promoted to governor of Anhui.
units.literal: In the sixth year he was promoted to Governor of Anhui.

units.zh: 廷楨疏言：「悍俗誠宜重懲，婦女顧名節，多自殘求免，或自盡傷生，情在可矜，請停其例。」
units.en: Deng memorialized: 'These violent customs deserve harsh punishment, but women mindful of their reputation often mutilate themselves to avoid banishment, or take their own lives. Their plight deserves compassion, and I ask that this regulation be suspended.'
units.literal: Deng submitted a memorial saying: 'The fierce custom truly deserves severe punishment, but women, mindful of chastity, often mutilate themselves to seek exemption, or kill themselves and harm their lives; the circumstances deserve compassion—please suspend this regulation.'

units.zh: 廷楨疏陳，略曰：「臣緝懲鴉片，三載於茲。
units.en: Deng memorialized in summary: 'I have pursued and punished the opium trade for three years now.
units.literal: Deng submitted a memorial stating in summary: 'Your servant has pursued and punished opium for three years now.

units.zh: 豪猾之徒，刑僇逋逃，身家既失，怨讟遂興。
units.en: Powerful ruffians, punished and driven into flight, have lost their fortunes and now vent their resentment in slander.
units.literal: Crafty and powerful men, punished and fleeing, having lost their families and property, then gave rise to resentment and slander.

units.zh: 查檢為希旨，掩捕為貪功，偵伺為詭謀，推​​鞫為酷罰。
units.en: Inspections are called currying favor; secret arrests, greed for credit; surveillance, conspiracy; and forced confessions, cruel punishment.
units.literal: Inspections are called currying favor, secret arrests are called greed for merit, surveillance is called scheming, and interrogation under torture is called cruel punishment.

units.zh: 誣以納賄，目以營私。
units.en: They accuse us of taking bribes and pursuing private profit.
units.literal: They falsely accuse us of taking bribes and label us as seeking private gain.

units.zh: 譏建議為急於理財，訾新例為輕於改律，狂悖紛熒，無非為煙匪洩憤。」
units.en: They mock the policy as a rush to raise revenue and denounce the new regulations as reckless changes to the law—all of it nothing but the opium traffickers venting their rage.'
units.literal: They mock the proposal as haste to raise revenue, denounce the new regulations as lightly changing the law, and their wild and rebellious clamor is nothing but venting by opium criminals.'

units.zh: 以獲南河掘堤首犯陳端，詔嘉獎。
units.en: He won imperial commendation for capturing Chen Duan, ringleader of the Southern River dike-breach conspiracy.
units.literal: Because he captured Chen Duan, ringleader of the Southern River dike-breach case, an edict commended and rewarded him.

units.zh: 十六年，英吉利商人以躉船載煙，廷楨禁止不許進口，猶泊外洋，嚴旨驅逐。
units.en: In 1836 British merchants used receiving ships to store opium offshore. Deng barred import, but the ships remained at anchor in outer waters until stern edicts ordered them driven away.
units.literal: In the sixteenth year British merchants used receiving ships to carry opium; Deng forbade import, yet they still anchored in outer waters, and stern edicts ordered their expulsion.

units.zh: 廷楨與提督關天培整備海防，迭於大嶼山口、急水洋獲蟹艇，載銀鉅萬，盡數充賞，破獲囤煙私販。
units.en: Deng and Provincial Commander Guan Tianpei strengthened coastal defenses, repeatedly seizing smuggling boats at Dayushankou and Jishuiyang laden with tens of thousands of taels of silver. The confiscated funds were distributed as rewards, and they broke up opium stockpiles and illicit trafficking rings.
units.literal: Deng together with Provincial Commander Guan Tianpei prepared coastal defenses, repeatedly at Dayushankou and Jishuiyang captured smuggling boats carrying tens of thousands of taels of silver, confiscated all as reward funds, and broke up stockpiled opium and private trafficking.

units.zh: 十八年，英船載屬番男婦五百餘人赴澳門居住，驅令回國。
units.en: In 1838 British ships brought more than five hundred dependent natives, men and women, to settle at Macao. Deng ordered them sent home.
units.literal: In the eighteenth year British ships carried more than five hundred dependent natives, men and women, to live at Macao; he drove them to return to their country.

units.zh: 十九年，林則徐奉命至廣東，廷楨與之同心協力，盡獲躉船積煙，焚之，嚴私販之罪；
units.en: In 1839 Lin Zexu arrived in Guangdong on imperial orders. Deng worked with him in full concert, seized all opium stored on receiving ships and burned it, and imposed severe penalties on smugglers;
units.literal: In the nineteenth year Lin Zexu was ordered to Guangdong; Deng worked with him in full accord, seized all opium stockpiled on receiving ships, burned it, and strictly punished private trafficking;

units.zh: 臨以兵威，屢戰皆捷，事詳則徐傳。
units.en: backed the policy with military force and won repeated victories. The details are given in Lin's biography.
units.literal: faced them with military force, and won victory in repeated battles—the details are given in Lin's biography.

units.zh: 調兩江、雲貴，皆未赴，閩防方急，遂調閩浙總督。
units.en: He was transferred first to the Two Jiangs and then to Yunnan-Guizhou, but took neither post. With Fujian's defenses under pressure, he was made governor-general of Fujian and Zhejiang.
units.literal: He was transferred to the Two Jiangs and to Yunnan-Guizhou, but went to neither; as Fujian's defenses were urgent, he was then transferred to Governor-General of Fujian and Zhejiang.

units.zh: 二十年三月，英船窺廈門，遣提督程恩高等迎敵於梅林澳，擊走之。
units.en: In the third month of 1840 British ships probed Xiamen. He sent Provincial Commander Cheng En'gao and others to meet them at Meilin Bay and drive them off.
units.literal: In the third month of the twentieth year British ships spied on Xiamen; he dispatched Provincial Commander Cheng En'gao and others to meet the enemy at Meilin Bay and drive them off.

units.zh: 六月，敵船駛入廈門，求通貿易，阻之，遂開砲，來撲砲台，參將陳勝元、守備陳光福奮擊，斃其前隊數人，發砲傷敵甚眾，乃遁。
units.en: In the sixth month enemy ships entered Xiamen demanding trade. When refused, they opened fire and assaulted the batteries. Assistant Commander Chen Shengyuan and Garrison Commander Chen Guangfu fought back fiercely, killing several in the enemy vanguard and wounding many more with cannon fire until the enemy withdrew.
units.literal: In the sixth month enemy ships entered Xiamen seeking trade; blocked, they opened fire and came to assault the batteries; Assistant Commander Chen Shengyuan and Garrison Commander Chen Guangfu fought fiercely, killed several in the enemy vanguard, fired cannon and wounded many of the enemy, and they then fled.

units.zh: 九月，詔以廷楨等在粵辦理不善，轉滋事端，與林則徐同奪職。
units.en: In the ninth month an edict blamed Deng and his colleagues for mishandling affairs in Guangdong and provoking further trouble. He was dismissed from office together with Lin Zexu.
units.literal: In the ninth month an edict stated that Deng and others had handled affairs poorly in Guangdong and instead stirred up trouble, and they were dismissed from office together with Lin Zexu.

units.zh: 二十一年，琦善撤沿海兵備，虎門失守，复追論廷楨久任兩廣，廢弛營務，與則徐同戍伊犁。
units.en: In 1841 Qishan withdrew coastal defenses and Humen fell. Deng was again blamed for lax military administration during his long tenure in the Two Guang and was banished to Yili together with Lin.
units.literal: In the twenty-first year Qishan withdrew coastal defenses, Humen fell, and Deng was again held accountable for long service in the Two Guang and neglect of military affairs, and was exiled to Yili together with Lin.

units.zh: 二十三年，釋還。
units.en: In 1843 he was released and allowed to return.
units.literal: In the twenty-third year he was released and returned.

units.zh: 尋予三品頂戴，授甘肅布政使。
units.en: He was soon given third-rank insignia and appointed financial commissioner of Gansu.
units.literal: Soon afterward he was granted third-rank insignia and appointed Financial Commissioner of Gansu.

units.zh: 議清查荒地，親往歷勘，由銀州東盡洮、隴，西極酒泉，得田一萬九千四百餘頃，又番貢地一千五百餘頃，寧夏馬廠地歸公一百餘頃，熟地昇科，荒者招墾，詔嘉其勤，复二品頂戴。
units.en: When a survey of wasteland was proposed, he inspected the territory in person from Yinzhou east to the Tao and Long regions and west to Jiuquan. He identified more than 19,400 qing of fields, 1,500 qing of tribal tribute land, and more than 100 qing of Ningxia horse-pasture returned to the state. Cultivated land was brought onto the tax rolls and wasteland opened to settlers. The throne praised his diligence and restored his second-rank insignia.
units.literal: When a survey of wasteland was proposed, he personally went to inspect it; from Yinzhou east to the Tao and Long regions and west to Jiuquan, he found 19,400-odd qing of fields, plus 1,500-odd qing of tribute lands of tribes, and more than 100 qing of horse-pasture land in Ningxia returned to the state; cultivated land was brought onto the tax rolls and wasteland was opened for reclamation; an edict praised his diligence and restored his second-rank insignia.

units.zh: 二十五年，擢陝西巡撫，署陝甘總督。
units.en: In 1845 he was promoted to governor of Shaanxi and acted as governor-general of Shaanxi and Gansu.
units.literal: In the twenty-fifth year he was promoted to Governor of Shaanxi and served as acting Governor-General of Shaanxi and Gansu.

units.zh: 二十六年，卒於官。
units.en: In 1846 he died in office.
units.literal: In the twenty-sixth year he died in office.

units.zh: 子爾恆，亦官至陝西巡撫，自有傳。
units.en: His son Erheng also rose to governor of Shaanxi and has a biography of his own.
units.literal: His son Erheng also rose to Governor of Shaanxi and has his own biography.

units.zh: 廷楨治行早為時稱，屢躓屢起，宣宗知之深，故卒用之。
units.en: Deng's record in office had long been admired. Though he fell and rose again more than once, Emperor Xuanzong knew him well and in the end continued to use him.
units.literal: Deng's administrative conduct had long been praised in his time; though he stumbled and rose repeatedly, Emperor Xuanzong understood him deeply and therefore ultimately employed him again.

units.zh: 六月，英船至廈門，為閩浙總督鄧廷楨所拒。
units.en: In the sixth month British ships reached Xiamen and were turned back by Governor-General Deng Tingzhen of Fujian and Zhejiang.
units.literal: In the sixth month British ships reached Xiamen and were repelled by Governor-General of Fujian and Zhejiang Deng Tingzhen.

units.zh: 廣東瑤匪趙仔青竄入湖南，率提督餘步雲、總兵曾勝追剿之；
units.en: When the Guangdong Yao rebel Zhao Zaiqing fled into Hunan, he led Yu Buyun and Zeng Sheng in pursuit;
units.literal: The Yao bandit Zhao Zaiqing from Guangdong fled into Hunan; he led Provincial Commander Yu Buyun and Regional Commander Zeng Sheng in pursuit;

units.zh: 遣步雲、勝等先後破賊，擒首逆鄧三、盤文理，毀其巢。
units.en: He sent Buyun and Sheng to rout the rebels, capture leaders Deng San and Pan Wenli, and destroy their strongholds.
units.literal: He sent Buyun, Sheng, and others in succession to defeat the bandits, capture the ringleaders Deng San and Pan Wenli, and destroy their lairs.

units.zh: 高宗又以舊記星紀，間有疏漏，御製璣衡撫辰儀，重加測候。
units.en: Qianlong, finding gaps in older star catalogs, built the Armillary Sphere and Chronographic Instrument and remeasured the sky.
units.literal: The Gaozong Emperor again, because old star records had occasional gaps, personally made the Armillary Sphere and Chronographic Instrument and took new observations.

units.zh: 乾隆六十年以後，國史無徵，則從闕焉。
units.en: After Qianlong 60 the Veritable Records offer no material, so the account stops there.
units.literal: After Qianlong year 60 the National History has no testimony, and those years are therefore omitted.

units.zh: 今以康熙年間實測各省及諸蒙古高度、偏度，並乾隆時憲所增省分，與回疆部落、兩金川土司等，晝夜永短，節氣早晚，推得高度、偏度備列焉。
units.en: Here Kangxi surveys, Qianlong additions, Xinjiang, and Jinchuan observations yield revised polar altitudes and longitudinal offsets.
units.literal: Now from Kangxi-era actual surveys of each province and Mongol banners, plus provinces added in the Qianlong Time Constitution, together with Muslim borderland tribes and the two Jinchuan chieftaincies — day and night length, solar-term timing — heights and offsets are derived and fully listed.

units.zh: 有清統一區夏，聖聖相承。
units.en: The Qing unified China, one sage emperor following another.
units.literal: The Qing unified All-under-Heaven, sage succeeding sage.

units.zh: 迨平定回疆及兩金川，復令重度裏差，增入時憲。
units.en: After pacifying Xinjiang and the two Jinchuan campaigns, he ordered li-cha remeasured and entered into the Shixian calendar.
units.literal: When the Muslim borderlands and the Two Jinchuan were pacified, he again ordered remeasurement of li-cha and added the results to the Time Constitution calendar.

units.zh: 其後禧恩之徵瑤，奕山、奕經之防海，或以驕侈召謗，或以輕率僨事。
units.en: After that, Xi'en's campaign against the Yao and the coastal defense efforts of Yishan and Yijing brought censure through arrogance and extravagance in some cases and failure through rashness in others.
units.literal: Afterward, in Xi'en's campaign against the Yao, and in Yishan and Yijing's coastal defense, some invited censure through arrogance and extravagance, others ruined affairs through rashness.

units.zh: 金釗素不附和議，與穆彰阿等意齟《齒吾》。
units.en: Jinzhao had never favored appeasement and was at odds with Muzhanga and others.
units.literal: Jinzhao had never favored the appeasement faction and was at odds with Muzhanga and others.

units.zh: 積數歲，永始中，相禹奏立對外家怨望，有惡言。
units.en: Years later, in the Yongshi era, Chancellor Yu impeached Li for muttering slander against his in-laws.
units.literal: Accumulating several years, in the Yongshi period, Chancellor Yu memorialized that Li, toward his wife’s kin, bore resentment and had evil words.

units.zh: 時為固原知州徐采饒等所訐，命協辦大學士祁俊藻往會總督琦善按之，坐關防不密、清查歧誤，及失察家人，議降調革任。
units.en: He was then denounced by Guyuan prefect Xu Cairao and others; Associate Grand Secretary Qi Junzao joined Governor-General Qishan in an inquiry; lax seals, audit mistakes, and unchecked servants earned a sentence of demotion and dismissal.
units.literal: At that time he was impeached by Guyuan prefect Xu Cairao and others; Associate Grand Secretary Qi Junzao was sent to join Governor-General Qishan in investigation; he was found guilty of lax seal control, errors in audit, and failure to supervise his household, and was sentenced to demotion, dismissal, and forfeiture.

units.zh: 二十九年，因病請罷，許之。
units.en: In the twenty-ninth year he sought release for illness and was allowed to retire.
units.literal: In the twenty-ninth year [1849], he asked to resign on account of illness and was permitted.

units.zh: 府尹曾望顏請罷各國通商，禁漁船出洋。
units.en: Prefect Zeng Wangyan proposed cutting off trade with all nations and banning fishing boats from going to sea.
units.literal: Prefect Zeng Wangyan requested that trade with all countries be stopped and fishing boats forbidden to go to sea.

units.zh: 敵軍近逼通州，乃改命怡親王載垣、尚書穆廕往議，誘擒英官巴夏禮置之獄，而我軍屢敗之餘不能戰，車駕倉猝幸熱河，廷臣爭之不可。
units.en: When the enemy neared Tongzhou, Prince Yi Zaiyuan and Minister Mu Yin were sent instead; they tricked and seized the British envoy Parkes and put him in prison. But with our forces already beaten repeatedly we could not fight on; the court fled in haste to Rehe, and ministers' protests availed nothing.
units.literal: As the enemy army pressed close to Tongzhou, the order was changed and Prince Yi Zaiyuan and Minister Mu Yin were sent to negotiate; they lured and seized the British official Parkes and imprisoned him; yet after repeated defeats our army could not fight; the imperial carriage hastily proceeded to Rehe; court ministers protested in vain.

units.zh: 十年，英法聯軍又來犯，僧格林沁拒戰屢失利，復遣桂良等議和。
units.en: In 1860 the allied armies returned; Sengge Rinchen fought them repeatedly but lost again and again, and Guiliang and others were once more dispatched to negotiate.
units.literal: In the tenth year the Anglo-French allied forces came again; Sengge Rinchen resisted repeatedly but suffered defeat after defeat; Guiliang and others were again sent to negotiate.

units.zh: 肅順九月壬午遷。瑞常理藩院尚書。十二月庚午遷。穆蔭理藩院尚書。
units.en: On the renwu day of the ninth month, Sushun was transferred. Ruichang: Minister of the Court of Colonial Affairs. On the gengwu day of the twelfth month, was transferred. Muyin: Minister of the Court of Colonial Affairs.
units.literal: On the renwu day of the ninth month, Sushun was transferred. Ruichang: Minister of the Court of Colonial Affairs. On the gengwu day of the twelfth month, was transferred. Muyin: Minister of the Court of Colonial Affairs.

units.zh: 咸豐八年戊午
units.en: Eighth year of Xianfeng (1858), wuwu
units.literal: Eighth year of Xianfeng, wuwu

units.zh: 穆蔭十二月壬寅遷。春佑理藩院尚書。
units.en: On the renyin day of the twelfth month, Muyin was transferred. Chunyou: Minister of the Court of Colonial Affairs.
units.literal: On the renyin day of the twelfth month, Muyin was transferred. Chunyou: Minister of the Court of Colonial Affairs.

units.zh: 咸豐九年己未
units.en: Ninth year of Xianfeng (1859), jiwei
units.literal: Ninth year of Xianfeng, jiwei

units.zh: 僅予大學士桂良等鐫級留任，出考堂官罰俸而已。
units.en: Only Grand Secretary Gui Liang and others lost a rank increment while retaining office; inspecting chiefs received only salary fines.
units.literal: Only Grand Secretary Gui Liang and others had a rank inscription removed but were retained; the chiefs who conducted the inspection were merely fined.

units.zh: 咸豐十年，刑部堂官濫保不諳例案之員，朝廷務循寬大，輒以相習成風，不獨刑部為然，多為原宥。
units.en: In Xianfeng 10 (1860), Ministry of Justice chiefs recommended officials ignorant of legal precedent; the court's habitual leniency extended across ministries, and most offenders were pardoned.
units.literal: In the tenth year of Xianfeng, Ministry of Justice chiefs recklessly recommended staff ignorant of case precedents; the court pursued leniency, and this became habitual—not only in the Ministry of Justice; most were pardoned.

units.zh: 十八年，鴻臚寺卿黃爵滋請禁鴉片煙，下中外大臣議。
units.en: In 1838 Huang Juezi, grand secretary of the Court of State Ceremonial, memorialized for a ban on opium, and the throne ordered ministers throughout the empire to discuss the proposal.
units.literal: In the eighteenth year Grand Secretary of the Court of State Ceremonial Huang Juezi requested a ban on opium, and the matter was referred for discussion to ministers at home and abroad.

units.zh: 巡撫王有齡速即會同王履謙妥為勸辦，議定章程，不得徇私委派貪劣之員。」
units.en: Governor Wang Youling was ordered to work with Wang Luqian at once, organize donations properly, set clear regulations, and appoint no corrupt or unworthy men out of favoritism.'
units.literal: Governor Wang Youling was ordered quickly to consult with Wang Luqian and properly organize solicitation, draw up regulations, and not assign corrupt or inferior officials out of favoritism.'

units.zh: 令王有齡會同王履謙切實籌辦，以固疆圉。
units.en: Wang Youling was ordered to work with Wang Luqian and organize matters in earnest to secure the frontier.
units.literal: Wang Youling was ordered to consult with Wang Luqian and earnestly organize affairs to strengthen the frontier.

units.zh: 二十一年，調署湖北，以陳宏謀代焯。
units.en: In 1756 he was transferred to act as governor of Hubei, with Chen Hongmou slated to replace him.
units.literal: In the twenty-first year he was transferred to act in Hubei, with Chen Hongmou replacing Chao.

units.zh: 宏謀未至，上命發歸化城米運金川饋軍，急驛諭宏謀。
units.en: Before Hongmou arrived, the throne ordered grain from Guihua City shipped to supply the Jinchuan campaign and sent an urgent courier to inform Hongmou.
units.literal: Before Hongmou arrived, the emperor ordered grain from Guihua City sent to provision the army in Jinchuan, urgently dispatching a courier to instruct Hongmou.

units.zh: 前巡撫耆齡、御史華祝三復劾崇光任用非人，調度乖方，詔命自陳，下署總督晏端書、提督昆壽察按，得免議。
units.en: Former governor Qiling and censor Hua Zhu again impeached Chongguang for employing unfit persons and erratic command; an edict ordered him to explain himself; acting governor-general Yan Duanshu and military commander Kunshou were sent to investigate, and he was cleared of charges.
units.literal: The former governor Qiling and Censor Hua Zhu again impeached Chongguang for employing unfit persons and erratic command; an edict ordered him to explain himself; Acting Governor-General Yan Duanshu and Military Commander Kunshou were sent to investigate, and he was cleared of charges.

units.zh: 御史陳慶鏞疏論僨事諸臣罪狀，上重違清議，再褫琦善職，意仍鄉用，未幾，予三等侍衛，充駐藏大臣。
units.en: Censor Chen Qingyong listed the crimes of the officials who had mishandled the crisis. Bowing to public opinion, the emperor stripped Qi Shan of office again, though he still meant to use him. Soon he was made a third-class bodyguard and resident commissioner in Tibet.
units.literal: Censor Chen Qingyong memorialized on the crimes of the officials involved in the affair; the emperor, giving weight to pure opinion, again stripped Qi Shan of office, though he still intended to employ him; before long he was given the rank of third-class bodyguard and appointed resident commissioner in Tibet.

units.zh: 良弼，字賚臣，紅帶子，隸鑲黃旗，大學士伊里布孫。
units.en: Liang Bi, styled Baichen, was a girdled bannerman enrolled in the Bordered Yellow Banner and a grandson of Grand Secretary Yilibu.
units.literal: Liang Bi, styled Baichen, was a girdled bannerman of the Bordered Yellow Banner and grandson of the Grand Secretary Yilibu.

units.zh: 死未旬日，而遜位詔下，時皆悼之。
units.en: Within ten days of his death the abdication edict was promulgated, and contemporaries mourned him all the more.
units.literal: Less than ten days after his death the abdication edict was issued, and all mourned him.

units.zh: 少孤，事母孝。
units.en: Orphaned early, he was devoted to his mother.
units.literal: He lost his father young and served his mother with filial devotion.

units.zh: 季芝昌五月乙巳遷。朱鳳標左都御史。
units.en: On the yisi day of the fifth month, Ji Zhichang was transferred. Zhu Fengbiao: Left Censor-in-Chief.
units.literal: On the yisi day of the fifth month, Ji Zhichang was transferred. Zhu Fengbiao: Left Censor-in-Chief.

units.zh: 咸豐元年辛亥
units.en: First year of Xianfeng (1851), xinhai
units.literal: First year of Xianfeng, xinhai

units.zh: 朱鳳標
units.en: Zhu Fengbiao.
units.literal: Zhu Fengbiao.

units.zh: 朱鳳標
units.en: Zhu Fengbiao.
units.literal: Zhu Fengbiao.

units.zh: 朱鳳標二月己卯遷。周祖培左都御史。十一月庚寅遷。許乃普左都御史。
units.en: On the jimao day of the second month, Zhu Fengbiao was transferred. Zhou Zupei: Left Censor-in-Chief. On the gengyin day of the eleventh month, was transferred. Xu Naipu: Left Censor-in-Chief.
units.literal: On the jimao day of the second month, Zhu Fengbiao was transferred. Zhou Zupei: Left Censor-in-Chief. On the gengyin day of the eleventh month, was transferred. Xu Naipu: Left Censor-in-Chief.

units.zh: 咸豐四年甲寅
units.en: Fourth year of Xianfeng (1854), jiayin
units.literal: Fourth year of Xianfeng, jiayin

units.zh: 張芾革。五月甲寅朱鳳標左副都御史。十二月丙戌遷。
units.en: Zhang Fei was dismissed. On the jiayin day of the fifth month, Zhu Fengbiao: Left Deputy Censor-in-Chief. On the bingxu day of the twelfth month, was transferred.
units.literal: Zhang Fei was dismissed. On the jiayin day of the fifth month, Zhu Fengbiao: Left Deputy Censor-in-Chief. On the bingxu day of the twelfth month, was transferred.

units.zh: 咸豐十年庚申
units.en: Tenth year of Xianfeng (1860), gengshen
units.literal: Tenth year of Xianfeng, gengshen

units.zh: 因御史蘇廷魁奏英吉利為鄰國所破，詔促耆英赴廣州本任，乘機進剿，尋知其訛傳，仍留浙江。
units.en: When Censor Su Tingkui reported that Britain had been defeated by its neighbors, the court ordered Qiying to Guangzhou to exploit the chance to attack. The story proved false, and he stayed in Zhejiang.
units.literal: Because Censor Su Tingkui memorialized that England had been broken by neighboring states, an edict urged Qiying to proceed to his proper post at Guangzhou and seize the chance to attack; it was soon learned to be false report, and he remained in Zhejiang.

units.zh: 二十二年正月，粵事急，琦善既黜，調耆英廣州將軍，授欽差大臣，督辦浙江洋務。
units.en: In the first month of 1842, with Guangdong in crisis and Qi Shan dismissed, Qiying was made general of Guangzhou, imperial commissioner, and supervisor of foreign affairs in Zhejiang.
units.literal: In the first month of the twenty-second year, when Guangdong affairs grew urgent and Qi Shan had been dismissed, Qiying was transferred to general of Guangzhou, appointed imperial commissioner, and put in charge of foreign affairs in Zhejiang.

units.zh: 檄諭英國領事義律查繳煙土，驅逐躉船，呈出煙土二萬餘箱，親蒞虎門驗收，焚於海濱，四十餘日始盡。
units.en: He ordered British consul Charles Elliot to surrender all opium and expel the receiving ships. More than 20,000 chests were turned over; Lin personally supervised their receipt at Humen and had them burned on the shore, a process that took more than forty days to complete.
units.literal: He issued a proclamation instructing British Consul Elliot to investigate and surrender opium, expel the receiving ships, and present more than 20,000 chests of opium; he personally went to Humen to inspect the receipt, and it was burned on the seashore, taking more than forty days to finish.

units.zh: 他國皆聽命，獨義律枝梧未從。
units.en: Merchants of other nations complied, but Elliot alone stalled and refused.
units.literal: Other countries all obeyed; only Elliot prevaricated and did not comply.

units.zh: 義律請令赴澳門載貨，冀囤煙私販，嚴斥拒之，潛泊尖沙嘴外洋。
units.en: Elliot asked to be allowed to load cargo at Macao, evidently intending to stockpile opium for illicit sale. Lin refused him sharply, and Elliot lay at anchor secretly off Chunshui Tsui.
units.literal: Elliot requested permission to go to Macao to load cargo, hoping to hoard opium for private sale; Lin sternly rejected this, and Elliot secretly anchored in the outer waters off Chunshui Tsui.

units.zh: 七月，義律藉索食為名，以貨船載兵犯九龍山砲台，參將賴恩爵擊走之。
units.en: In the seventh month Elliot, claiming he needed provisions, sent merchant ships carrying troops against the Kowloon Hill battery. Assistant Commander Lai Enjue repulsed them.
units.literal: In the seventh month Elliot, under the pretext of seeking food, used merchant ships to carry troops and attacked the Kowloon Hill battery; Assistant Commander Lai Enjue drove them off.

units.zh: 七月，義律至天津，投書總督琦善，言廣東燒煙之釁，起自則徐及鄧廷楨二人，索價不與，又遭詬逐，故越境呈訴。
units.en: In the seventh month Elliot reached Tianjin and wrote to Governor Qishan, blaming Lin and Deng Tingzhen for the Guangdong opium burning, claiming they had refused compensation and driven him out, and had therefore come north to petition.
units.literal: In the seventh month Elliot reached Tianjin and sent a letter to Governor Qishan, saying that the provocation of burning opium in Guangdong originated with Lin and Deng Tingzhen; they would not agree to compensation and moreover subjected him to abuse and expulsion, so he crossed the border to lodge his complaint.

units.zh: 英兵犯浙江，定海、鎮海及寧波府城相繼陷，裕謙死事，命為揚威將軍，督師往剿，都統哈哴阿、提督胡超為參贊，尋易侍郎文蔚、都統特依順副之。
units.en: When the British invaded Zhejiang and Dinghai, Zhenhai, and Ningbo fell one after another, Yu Qian died in the fighting. Yijing was named Campaign General to lead the punitive force, with Ha'er'a and Hu Chao as deputies; before long Wen Wei and Te Yishun replaced them.
units.literal: When the English army attacked Zhejiang, Dinghai, Zhenhai, and the prefectural city of Ningbo fell in succession and Yu Qian died in service, he was ordered to serve as Campaign General, commanding troops to suppress the enemy, with Banner Commander Ha'er'a and Provincial Military Commander Hu Chao as deputies; soon Minister Wen Wei and Banner Commander Te Yishun replaced them as deputies.

units.zh: 文蔚，費莫氏，滿洲正藍旗人。
units.en: Wen Wei, of the Feimo clan, belonged to the Manchu Plain Blue Banner.
units.literal: Wen Wei, of the Feimo clan, was a Manchu of the Plain Blue Banner.

units.zh: 文蔚聞敗亦退，軍資器械棄失殆盡。
units.en: Hearing of the defeat, Wen Wei withdrew as well, leaving nearly all supplies and weapons behind.
units.literal: Wen Wei, hearing of the defeat, also withdrew; military stores and weapons were abandoned almost entirely.

units.zh: 嘉慶二年進士，授翰林院檢討。
units.en: He passed the metropolitan examination in the second year of Jiaqing and became a Hanlin compiler.
units.literal: A metropolitan graduate in the second year of Jiaqing, he was appointed Hanlin Compiler.

units.zh: 方其駐長谿嶺也，聞諸路軍皆不利，欲移營走。
units.en: While he held Changxi Ridge and heard that every column had failed, he wanted to break camp and run.
units.literal: While he was encamped at Changxi Ridge, hearing that every column had fared badly, he wished to move camp and flee.

units.zh: 敵雜難民潰兵猝至，焚毀營帳，乃奔曹娥江，收集潰兵，退保紹興。
units.en: Enemy troops mixed with refugees and fugitives struck suddenly, burned his camp, and he fled to the Cao'e, rallied what he could, and fell back on Shaoxing.
units.literal: The enemy mixed with refugees and routed troops arrived suddenly, burned the camp, and he fled to the Cao'e River, gathered the fugitives, and withdrew to defend Shaoxing.

units.zh: 尋以定海報捷，加頭品頂戴。
units.en: Soon he received the first-rank ruby button for the reported victory at Dinghai.
units.literal: Soon, on the reported victory at Dinghai, he was given the ruby button of the first rank.

units.zh: 軍事竣，追論失機，褫職下獄。
units.en: When the campaign ended he was prosecuted for missing his chance, stripped of rank, and jailed.
units.literal: When military affairs ended, lost opportunities were pursued in review; he was stripped of office and imprisoned.

units.zh: 咸豐初，歷喀喇沙爾、哈密辦事大臣，駐藏大臣，奉天府尹。
units.en: Early in Xianfeng he served as commissioner at Karashahr and Hami, imperial commissioner in Tibet, and prefect of Fengtian.
units.literal: At the beginning of Xianfeng he served successively as Commissioner at Karashahr and Hami, Resident Commissioner in Tibet, and Prefect of Fengtian.

units.zh: 五年，卒。
units.en: He died in the fifth year.
units.literal: In the fifth year he died.
